# The Losee Center Rooftop — The Perch, and What Was and Was Not Recovered There

**File ID:** `LOSEE-E01` *(newly assigned by this revision — see revision log note. The topic folders have not previously carried File IDs; if the convention is unwanted, strike the line and nothing else changes.)*

**Scope:** everything the banked preliminary-hearing record says about the rooftop of Utah Valley University's **Losee Center** — how the roof is reached, what an officer found on it, what the crime lab processed there, the sight line to the tent, the northeast drop point, and, centrally, **what was searched for and not found**. It covers the roof and its immediate ground. It does **not** cover the rifle recovery in the wooded area, the DNA analysis as a subject, the arrest chronology, or the media narratives — those have their own folders and are pointed to, not duplicated.

**Case context:** *State of Utah v. Tyler James Robinson*, Case No. 251403576, Fourth Judicial District Court, Provo — Hon. **Tony F. Graf, Jr.** The preliminary hearing sat **2026-07-06 through 2026-07-13** (five hearing days). **Tyler Robinson is presumed innocent and, as of 2026-08-01, has NOT been bound over for trial.** A preliminary hearing tests **probable cause only**. The hearing adjourned **without any probable-cause determination**; the State's opening brief was due 2026-07-28, the defense response 2026-08-11, the State's reply 2026-08-18, with oral argument set for **2026-09-01 at 10:00 a.m.** (canonical at CR-ACQ §5.1). **No court has found any fact in this file to be true.** Everything below is **what a witness said under oath**, recorded faithfully and adopted by no one.

**Living persons — read before using anything below.**
- Allegations here are **attributed, never adopted**.
- **Lance Twiggs** testified under **use immunity** from both the Utah County Attorney's Office and the United States Attorney's Office and **is not accused of any offence in this record**. **Matthew Robinson** and **Amber Robinson** appear only as **elimination-sample donors** — persons whose profiles are obtained precisely so they can be accounted for and set aside — and **neither is accused of anything whatever.**
- **A DNA "support for inclusion" or "included as a possible contributor" statement is NOT a source attribution.** Both testifying DNA analysts said so expressly, and one agreed that a headline of the form "X's DNA was found on this item" **"would not be scientifically defensible."** **Nothing in this file says that anyone's DNA "was found on" anything, and nothing here may be re-stated in that form.** *(This is a live correction: the superseded stub used exactly that forbidden formulation — §2, row 8.)*
- Officers, deputies and lab staff are named only in their professional capacities and only where the record names them in open court. **No private individual's address, telephone number, or other contact or location detail appears here**, including details spoken aloud in open court (Day 1 contains such details; they are recorded as an event at CR-E05 §1.4 and reproduced nowhere).

**Prepared:** August 1, 2026
**Status:** **v1.0.** **This file REPLACES the previous `losee-rooftop-firing-evidence.md` of July 9, 2026** — a 62-line file built entirely from news reporting, with no primary sourcing. **§2 states, claim by claim, what was retained, corrected, refuted and withdrawn.** Findings below rest on **CR-E05 v1.1, which is VERIFIED**, on CR-E02 / CR-E03 / CR-E04, and on **fifteen direct verification searches run against the banked transcripts on 2026-08-01** (§1.1). **Nothing marked `[PROVISIONAL]` in any source file has been carried into this one** — see §1.6 for the list of what that excluded.

---

**Headline results — four.**

1. **The strongest form of the no-casing finding is now on the record, and it is a *purposive* negative.** The first officer onto the roof, **Officer Christopher Bagley**, searched **specifically for a spent shell casing** — at the prone position, over the edge, "all over the place" — **and found none**, and he explained why he knew to look. A second witness, the scene commander, independently said no bullets or casings were found on the roof or immediately around the building. **This is not a gap in the record; it is a search that returned nothing.** (§6)
2. **Nothing in the five banked hearing days establishes a discharge *at that location*.** Full-text searches of all five transcripts return **zero** occurrences of *gunshot residue / GSR / primer residue*, **zero** of *trajectory*, and **zero** of *reconstruct*. The rooftop case is **positional and circumstantial** — a gravel impression, a sight line, video of a prone figure, a screwdriver, a shoe imprint — and the record contains **no forensic test of the roof surface for a firing event at all.** This is a claim about these transcripts, not about the world (§6.2).
3. **The sight line was conceded and immediately qualified in the same breath.** Asked whether there is "a clear line of sight between the tent and the top of the Losee Center," Bagley answered "Yes, there is" — and on the **very next question** agreed some of it is **obstructed** by the Sorensen Center, confining the tent sight line to **"the far south side of the Losee building."** That is **the same portion of the roof where he independently found the gravel impression.** The coherence cuts for the State; the fact that it is a **lay eyeball estimate from photographs**, by a witness who expressly **was not a sniper**, cuts the other way. Both are logged (§5).
4. **The perch is an investigative *belief*; the distances are measurements; and the measurements' provenance is unestablished.** Sgt. Faumuina described "**what we believe was the shooter's perch**," identified at night by **oblique lighting** showing gravel disturbance, and gave **approximately 415 ft slope / 410 ft horizontal / 68 ft vertical** from perch to tent. The three figures are one internally consistent survey (√(410²+68²) ≈ 415.6). **But no witness said who took those measurements, when, or by what method** — a targeted search of Day 4 returns no such testimony. **Grade the perch identification and the geometry separately, always** (§4.3).

---

## 0. Sourcing framework (project standard)

- **Tier 1** — sworn testimony and primary court filings / primary documents
- **Tier 2** — named official statements (including named first-person statements by principals)
- **Tier 3** — named journalistic reporting/analysis
- **Tier 4** — anonymous-source or low-verification material

**"T1 via T3"** marks primary-document content known only through reporting; it is never silently promoted. **Sworn testimony is Tier 1 as to what the witness said, never automatically as to the world.** Two standing rules apply throughout: **a quotation by an interested party is reliable as to the words, not as to the document** (CR-ACQ §0); and **a forensic report is silent about the provenance of what it examined** (CR-AUDIT §4). **"— (checkable)"** marks items that are verifiable but not yet verified; they feed §12 and are **never counted as findings.**

**Confidence grades:** High / Medium-high / Medium / Low / unverified. **Every grade below traces to a verification act by this project**, named at the point of use — either a search run on **2026-08-01** and listed at §1.1, or the verified read recorded in CR-E05 v1.1.

*(Tier 1 as to what the witness said. **This project has not independently verified UVU's campus layout** — that is **— (checkable)** against a dated campus map or the admitted exhibits.)*

**Officer Christopher Bagley** — 26 years a police officer; on **2025-09-10** a senior officer with the **UVU Police Department** (five years there), previously Utah County Sheriff's Office, Springville City PD and Salt Lake County Sheriff's Office, with K-9, SWAT, motors, FTO and detective roles. **He did SWAT but expressly was not a sniper** — "I worked well with them, but I was not a sniper." ## 4. THE PERCH — recording layer

### 4.1 What the first officer saw, and how he qualified his own exhibit

Bagley reached the rooftop at **12:44** (his own recollection; `day1.txt` 01:43:05). He **hopped the guardrail** and, on the **southwest** side of the roof, found **a disturbance in the gravel**.

**His characterisation, verbatim** (`day1.txt` 02:26:12, stepping down to the monitor to explain **State's Exhibit 4**, a nighttime photograph):

> "To me, when I got up there and I could see this disturbance of gravel, to me, **it looks like a sniper pad, a person that has been laying in a prone position and you've got markings of elbows, knees, and feet** to where somebody was in the line of sight of where Charlie's tent was."

⚠ **His own qualification of the photographic evidence is preserved, because it is the single most important caveat on any rooftop image** (`day1.txt` 02:18:42–02:19:04, on **State's Exhibit 3.2**, the daytime view):

> **Q:** "And does this photograph do it justice?" — **A:** "**No.**"
> **Q:** "And how so?" — **A:** "You can't really see the impression I saw the time of when I was up there on that day. **I saw a distinct impression in the gravel and this does not show that.**"
> **Q:** "So you could see more with the naked eye?" — **A:** "Yes."

He located it on **State's Exhibit 2** as "the darker gray part… **the south side** of the Losee building… **on the southwest side of the roof**" (02:26:55). He **did not walk through or touch** the disturbance (02:41:17–02:41:25).

> **Analyst layer — recording and analyst layers held apart.** "**Sniper pad**" is **the witness's own word**, offered as an impression ("to me… to me"), by a witness who **expressly was not a sniper**. It is recorded with fidelity **and is adopted by nobody.** ⚠ **Any use of the rooftop photographs anywhere in this library must carry his "this does not show that."** The exhibits show *less* than the witness says he saw — which is a caution running **against** the images as proof of the impression, and simultaneously a fact **for** the State's account of what was on the roof. **Confidence: High** as to what he said (both passages read verbatim 2026-08-01). **What would change it:** the exhibits themselves, or any contemporaneous scene photograph or measurement of the impression.

### 4.2 How the crime lab identified and processed it

**Sgt. Jennifer Faumuina** (Utah DPS/SBI) was assigned on **2025-09-10 at approximately 1:30 p.m.** and identified **four scenes**: the amphitheatre; the Fulton Library (two bus stops); a wooded area; and **the Losee Center building and the ground below**. The rooftop was processed by the **Utah Bureau of Forensic Services** — the state crime lab (CR-E02 §2).

**Her account of the perch, verbatim** (`day4.txt` 04:35:59, verified directly 2026-08-01):

> "One item of evidence that was found was a screwdriver. Another one would've been **what we believe was the shooter's perch**. That was determined based… or that was **easy to see at night using oblique lighting**. We could see **disturbances in the gravel on the rear rooftop**. And then on the **northeast edge**, our team also found some **swipes on the ledge** of that rear rooftop, that was also collected."

Also on the rooftop: **shoe impressions** (04:38:28), collected along with the latent prints by those who processed the scene.

> **Analyst layer — the hedge is the witness's own and is preserved.** "**What we believe was**" is Faumuina's phrasing, not a hedge this file added. **The perch identification is an investigative conclusion drawn from a visual gravel disturbance**, corroborated by a second, earlier, independent observer (Bagley, hours before, in daylight, by naked eye). It is **not** a forensic determination that a firearm was discharged there. **Confidence: High** that both witnesses so testified. **Confidence that the disturbance was made by a person lying prone: Medium** — two lay/investigative visual identifications, no measurement, no cast, no comparison, and the primary photographic exhibit disclaimed by the witness who saw the original. **What would change it:** the scene photographs and the crime lab's processing notes; a cast or measurement of the impression; any comparison of the impression to a person or equipment.
> **Terminology note, logged and NOT treated as a conflict.** Faumuina says "**rear rooftop**"; Bagley says "**southwest**." She uses "rear rooftop" for **both** the gravel disturbance **and** the northeast-edge swipes, so on her usage it denotes the **upper roof generally**, not a compass direction. **No register entry is opened**; the two accounts are read as compatible, and the reading is stated so it can be checked.

## 5. THE SIGHT LINE — conceded, and qualified in the same breath

**Read verbatim from `day1.txt` 01:21:36–01:22:11** (verified directly 2026-08-01; the exchange is on a published State's exhibit, with the witness in the well of the court):

> **Q:** "Is there a **clear line of sight** between the tent and the top of the Losee Center? The rooftop?" — **A:** "**Yes, there is.**"
> **Q:** "Okay. **Is some of it obstructed?**" — **A:** "**Yes.**"
> **Q:** "Obstructed by what?" — **A:** "**The Sorenson building** that's right here, this white roof this kind of **obstructs a little bit of the view of the courtyard**."
> **Q:** "Where would you have to be standing or perhaps lying down on the Losee Center to see into the courtyard where that tent was?" — **A:** "**On the far south side of the Losee building, you could have a line of sight towards the courtyard**" — the **top roof**, the **darker shade of gray**.

He repeated it at the rooftop exhibits: of the **southwest** gravel area, "Is there a line of sight down into the courtyard?" — "**Yes, there is**" (02:18:19–02:18:25); and of the nighttime view, "you can see the tent in the grass area, **the direct line of sight** with the Sorenson building" (02:19:48).

> **Analyst layer — both directions, and no further.**
> **For the State, logged as squarely as anything against it:** the geometry and the physical scene **cohere from a single witness who was not asked to reconcile them and does not appear to have noticed.** The only part of the Losee roof he placed in view of the tent is the **far south / southwest** portion — **exactly where he independently found the gravel impression**. Coherence of that kind, arrived at obliquely, is a real evidentiary fact. **Confidence: High** as to what he said.
> **Available to the defence:** the "**clear line of sight**" answer was **immediately qualified on the State's own leading follow-up** as **partly obstructed by the Sorensen Center**, and the net effect of his answers is that the sight line to the tent was **confined to the far south portion** of the roof. This is a **lay eyeball estimate from photographs** — not a survey, not a measured sight-line reconstruction, not a trajectory analysis — from a witness who **expressly was not a sniper**. **The "clear line of sight" phrase must never be quoted without the next answer.**
> **What none of this establishes:** nothing here is evidence that a shot was fired, or from where. Equally — and this is an **over-hedge guard**, standing hazard 4 — **the Sorensen set-back does not imply that a rooftop shot was obstructed**: the Losee roof sits above the fourth level, and Bagley placed the Losee **in his own line of sight from the courtyard** when he inferred the shot's direction (§9.1). **Neither the "clear sight line" reading nor the "obstructed" reading is adopted here.**

I couldn't see one. I was looking over the edge, looking all over the place, making sure the gravel wasn't disturbed, and I couldn't find a shell casing at that moment.**"
> **Q:** "And that would be the reason you would be looking for that was because some types of guns when they shoot eject a casing automatically, right?" — **A:** "Yes."
> **Q:** "And then you also **didn't find any unshot bullets**?" — **A:** "**No.**"
> **Q:** "Are you aware of there being a bullet found on another roof… in the vicinity?" — **A:** "**I'm not aware.**"

### 6.4 What the absence of a roof casing does and does not mean

**It is consistent with the State's own theory of the weapon.** Faumuina testified to the mechanics: the rifle is **bolt action** — the user must manually work the bolt to load, lock and extract, unlike a semi-automatic that extracts and re-feeds on each trigger pull; **a spent case therefore remains in the chamber unless manually extracted.** And the fired case in evidence, **State's Exhibit 19, is "the cartridge case that was recovered from the gun," from the chamber** (`day4.txt` 04:55:45; CR-E02 §4). **On that account, no ejected casing would be expected on the roof at all.**

**But the same fact cuts the other way for the ballistic chain**, and this is the point the superseded file did not carry: **a fired case found *inside* a rifle is expected to identify to that rifle.** The ATF's `source identification` therefore links the case to the **weapon**, not the weapon to the **shooting**; and the only projectile evidence from the body — the **6A bullet jacket fragment** — was **inconclusive**. **Nothing recovered at the perch bears on it, because nothing was recovered at the perch.**

> **Analyst layer — FINDING 4.** **The absence of a casing on the roof is evidentially close to neutral**, and both halves must travel together. **It is not a hole in the State's case** (bolt-action mechanics explain it, and the chamber case is in evidence) **and it is not corroboration either** (a negative consistent with a theory does not confirm the theory; it merely fails to refute it). **What it does do is sharpen D-48**: the ATF firearms examination connects a case from the rifle's own chamber to the rifle, and **on this record the ATF firearms examination does not link the rifle to the shooting.** **Confidence: Medium-high** — the mechanics and the chamber recovery are Tier 1 testimony; **the ATF report itself has been read directly** (CR-ACQ §3.1), but the identity mapping of exhibit numbers across the two numbering systems is a well-supported **inference**, graded there and flagged as under challenge at Q-42 (human-gated). **The direction of D-48 is unaffected either way.**

## 7. THE NORTHEAST DROP POINT

**Bagley's first-hand account** (`day1.txt` 02:37:31–02:40:53, read verbatim 2026-08-01). After viewing UVU footage at the police department himself — "**look[ing] at the footage to verify for myself exactly what [t]ranspired**" — he saw an individual run to the edge, get up, run off, and **drop off the northeast side** of the Losee building. He then:

- went to the **northeast side** and found "**impressions of the shoe print inside the grass**" — later described as "**a shoe imprint that was embedded pretty deep right there next to where he dropped off**";
- looked **up onto the cement from the roof** and "could see **some scratching or rub marks** from the top of the roof **that was not there. I could see that looked abnormal**" *(rendered as Rev has it; the clause is garbled and is not smoothed)*;
- **taped off the whole area** — around trees, down to the back of the LDS Institute building — and **released the scene to two uniformed Payson police officers**, instructing them to admit no one but law enforcement or investigators. *(He released the **roof** scene separately, to a woman deputy sheriff — `day1.txt` 02:47:34.)*

He described the individual's route on **State's Exhibit 2**: prone at the **southwest**, then "came behind the… atrium… on the west side of it, came up to the north side of the Losee building on the east… and then he **dropped off on the east side** of the Losee building into the grass down here below" — confirmed on the next question as "**the northeast corner**."

**The crime lab's account** (Faumuina, `day4.txt` 04:36:27–04:37:11): the **northeast edge** is "the dropping off point." **Swipes** — "kind of hand marks or any type of marks that… is left by something that causes some type of disturbance" — were found "right on the edge of that rooftop. And then **right below we also had some other swipes as well, as well as some other impressions.** And then **below that was a glass window where we also located some latent prints.**"

**The fingerprint stipulation, read into the record as language agreed by both parties** (`day4.txt` 04:38:54; CR-E02 §3):

> The parties stipulate that investigators observed latent fingerprints and a palm print **on a glass window near the area where the individual landed** when the individual jumped from the rooftop of the Losee Center at UVU. SBI fingerprint examiner **Elisa Farmer** examined images of these and determined that **only three** of the latent prints — 11B, 11C and 11D — were of comparable or poor comparable value. **She excluded Tyler Robinson as the source of any of these three latent prints.**

**And the stipulation continues** — the part the superseded file did not have:

> Ms. Farmer reviewed other prints on the window and found they did not have adequate value for comparison. **Subsequent examinations of these three latent prints by the FBI were inconclusive.**

On direct, Faumuina testified that once investigators obtained footage **directly from UVU** they could zoom in, and: **"We determined that he was not — or he did not touch it."** On cross she confirmed the windows were processed **on September 11**, the day after, and that the purpose was precisely "to rule out whether the suspect had touched that window."

> **Analyst layer — FINDING 5, and a correction to this library's own earlier weighting.** The exclusion is **a real, stipulated fact agreed by both parties** and is recorded as such. **But it carries much less weight than it appears to**, for two independent reasons: the **FBI's re-examination of the same three prints was inconclusive**, so Farmer's exclusion is not the last word on them; and investigators concluded from better footage that **the person never touched the window at all**, which means **nobody's prints there were expected**. **An exclusion from prints the suspect is not believed to have left proves very little.**
> **Stated fairly in the other direction, because the "did not touch it" determination is what does the down-weighting:** that determination is an **investigative conclusion from video review, not a forensic finding**, and it rests on the quality of footage **this project has not seen**. **Confidence: High** that all three things were testified to; **Medium** that the exclusion carries little weight, since that assessment depends on the video determination being sound. **What would change it:** the footage itself, or Farmer's and the FBI's examination records. *(This correction was made in CR-E02 §3 and is carried here rather than re-litigated.)*

## 9. TIMING, CUSTODY, AND THE UNSECURED WINDOW

### 9.1 The shot, and the inference to the building

Bagley was posted on the Hall of Flags overlook when, a little after noon, "**A kid asked him a question, and then I heard a shot fired.**" He put it at **12:23**. He ran down, was told by radio within roughly a minute that "**we had a shooter in custody**" — his reaction: "**Oh, that was kind of fast.**" ⚠ **The person detained within ~30 seconds was detained in the courtyard, by the tent — not near the holster** — and this record never names that person.

While clearing the tiered grass to preserve evidence, standing beside Chief Long, he saw an **empty concealed-pistol holster** on the top grass tier: "**That's when things started slowing down for me a little bit.**" In that pause **he concluded the shot had been a rifle, not a handgun** — a handgun is "a short bang pop sound," a rifle "a longer violent bang or crackle sound." He knew the sound came from the **east**, and the **Losee building "was right in my" line of sight.**

⚠ **The holster was never collected.** He noticed no markings, has "**no idea**" what happened to it, never took custody of it, never told anyone else to, and "**just left it on the grass**." He does not know whether it was ever fingerprinted. **Recorded at the recording layer; no inference is drawn. It is an item of potential evidentiary interest, in a homicide, expressly left in place by the officer who found it.**

⚠ **His body camera died on the roof, before the tape went up.** The **27-minute-35-second** recording — starting at the Hall of Flags and ending while he was still on the roof — is **his only footage of that day**; he never docked it or restarted it: "too chaotic" (`day1.txt` 04:12:23–04:12:54, read verbatim 2026-08-01).

### 9.2 The window before the roof was secured — recorded in full, because it runs both ways

The full cross-examination exchange (`day1.txt` 04:09:09–04:10:46, read verbatim 2026-08-01). **CR-E05 §3.5 summarises this accurately but compresses it; the sequence is worth having whole**, because the witness gave three different-sounding answers in ninety seconds and counsel had to rephrase twice:

> **Q:** "did you check to see if anyone had been on the Losee building after the shooting after this individual had jumped off…? Was there anybody else on the roof? Did you check and see **in that gap of time**?"
> **A:** "**In that gap of time, no.** So once I put up the barrier, I only walked up to about that point. Then I went down and reviewed the video from that moment on."
> **Q:** "Are you able to say for one way or the other if anyone else had been on that roof in between when the person jumped off the building and when you came on the roof?"
> **A:** "**There was people up there looking for an individual that ran that way** because when I first got told the individual ran heading north, we didn't know where the shooter was. **So we started climbing up and looking, clearing the building.** And it wasn't until I went to the PD and I actually saw him jump off of the building that I knew he was off the building."
> *(Counsel rephrases.)* **Q:** "between that and when you got on the roof, did you ever check to see if anybody else had been on the roof in that period of time?"
> **A:** "**Yeah, and I didn't see anybody.**" … "**I didn't notice anybody.**"
> **Q:** "Did you look on the video to see that entire… So you did **not** review the video to see if there was someone between that individual jumping off and you coming on, if anybody had been on or disturbed that scene in any way?"

> **What is established:** **the video covering the window between the individual leaving the roof and Bagley's arrival was not reviewed**, and Bagley's own account is that **officers were climbing and clearing buildings during that window** in an active search for a shooter whose location was unknown.
