findings.why_it_matters: The file's stated purpose is that no headline figure may travel without its propositions. "Less than one in a trillion" is the most quotable and most misreadable figure Oliver gave — it is the form most easily mistaken for a source attribution, which is the very error §3.1 records her disclaiming — and the file omits the number entirely, so no downstream file can attach the qualification.

findings.claim_in_file: "⚠ The witness twice corrected counsel's 'you found his DNA' to 'there was support for inclusion,' with a likelihood ratio attached."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Her words were conditional, not indicative: "Correct. And there would have been a likelihood ratio statistic calculated and to go along with that." No numeric likelihood ratio for Matthew Robinson, Amber Robinson or Lance Twiggs is stated anywhere in Day 5 — not for item 1.4, not for 1.6, not for any Dremel swab. The magnitude of every elimination-donor result is entirely absent from the record. (Separately, the corrections number three, not two: at 1500, 1512 and 1536.)
findings.locator: day5.txt line 1528 ("would have been"); corrections at 1500, 1512, 1536; no LR value anywhere in day5.txt 1464–1560
findings.why_it_matters: Under the file's own living-persons header, "support for inclusion of Matthew Robinson... with a likelihood ratio attached" reads as though a quantified statistic backs the inclusion of two men who are not accused of anything. The record establishes the opposite: no magnitude was ever put in evidence. That absence is a scoped null the file should state, not a qualifier it should imply.

findings.claim_in_file: "⚠ Elimination samples were requested from the AGENTS involved in the case — standard practice because 'the type of testing we perform is quite sensitive' — and were NOT received."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The file cuts the operative half of her answer. In full: "The type of testing we perform is quite sensitive. So, it is a standard practice that we request elimination samples from any of the investigators involved in order to potentially eliminate them, IN CASE THEY COULD HAVE CONTAMINATED THE EVIDENCE." grep "contaminat" over CR-E06 returns 0.
findings.why_it_matters: Contamination control is the entire significance of the request and therefore of its non-receipt. Bolding "NOT received" while deleting the reason leaves the reader unable to see why it matters — and the deleted clause is the part that cuts against the State, so the omission is an unwarranted hedge, which this project treats as a reportable defect in its own right.

findings.claim_in_file: The §1.2 table asserts: label "Chad Grunander" (a prosecutor) = "Defence co-counsel, asking that a record be made with the livestream operators."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: No functional basis supports the reassignment, and the same transcript contradicts it. At 01:20:22 the court asks "And to the state?" and the answering turn is labelled "Chad Grunander" — "Yes." At 01:58:26 defence counsel invokes "Mr. Grunander's argument" as the State's earlier relevance argument. The 02:25:02 remark itself — "given the court's ruling this morning with respect to displaying exhibits, we may want to make a record with the live-streaming folks here that it's not going to be published" — is content-consistent with the State, which was the proponent of playing Exhibit 12.1 (raised by the prosecutor at 02:23:31). Nothing in the content announces it as defence.
findings.why_it_matters: This row sits in the table that finding 5.7 ("standing hazard 9 should be widened") rests on, and it violates the hazard it is illustrating: a person is named to a role without a stated basis, where label and content do not in fact disagree. A false entry in a warning about false attributions is the most corrosive kind of error in this file.

findings.claim_in_file: "No alternative, unconditioned likelihood ratio for Robinson was ever computed, offered, or even requested anywhere in Bakker's testimony... Confidence: High that the record is silent on the consequence."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: I tested this and the substance holds as a claim about the record: tsearch.py /without (assuming|Twiggs)|unconditioned|if you had not assumed|not used him as an elimination/ over day2.txt returns 0 hits (method self-validated). But "ever computed" is a claim about what happened inside the FBI laboratory, which no transcript can establish — and Bakker's own phrasing points the other way: "For ONE OF THE RUNS when I compared to Mr. Robinson conditioning on Mr. Twiggs, it was a 5% to 95%," which affirmatively implies other runs whose conditioning is nowhere enumerated on the record.
findings.locator: day2.txt line 6551; scoped null run 2026-08-01 over day2.txt
findings.why_it_matters: The file's own confidence line ("High that the RECORD is silent") is correctly scoped; the sentence above it is not, and it overreaches toward the State. §5.3 exists precisely to police unwarranted directionality, so an unscoped world-claim inside the over-hedge guard is self-undermining. The fix is one word: "appears on this record" for "was ever computed."

findings.claim_in_file: §8 item 5 turns on "the report counsel called 'Oliver 157'" and treats "Oliver 157" as a report designator; D-55 catalogues exhibit-identity failures. None of the designators 148, 154 or 156 appears anywhere in CR-E06.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The court stated on the record that these Day-5 numbers are numbers in the display application, not established exhibit numbers. Counsel asked outright, "Yeah, this is one... What's the exhibit on this?" and the court answered, "This is 154 in this application." The same series produces "Oliver 156" (the STRmix NGS material), "Exhibit Oliver 148" (the ATF SOP) and "report number 157... Oliver 157, which has been admitted" (counsel's assertion of admission, not a ruling read into the record).
findings.why_it_matters: D-55 is the register entry for exactly this defect, and §8 item 5 grades the bolt-swab identity question "Medium at best" on the strength of "Oliver 157" being a stable designator. The court's own statement that the numbering is application-internal is the strongest available evidence for D-55 and simultaneously weakens the premise of §8 item 5 — and it is absent.

findings.claim_in_file: "Extracts retained (swabs consumed, liquid remaining): 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.5, 1.7, 1.8, 1.13, 7.1 and 8.1." No comment follows on items 7.1 and 8.1.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Oliver's retained-extract list includes items designated 7.1 and 8.1 — the same designators as the FBI's item 7-1 (towel) and item 8-1 (screwdriver), the two items carrying the 1.7 octillion and 30 quintillion figures that are this file's headline. The transcript nowhere states whether these are the same physical items or a coincidence of a shared state evidence-numbering scheme.
findings.locator: day5.txt line 1039 (Oliver's list); day2.txt lines 4877 and 4913 (FBI items 7-1 and 8-1)
findings.why_it_matters: The file raises precisely this question for the rifle-bolt swab at §8 item 5 and treats designator collision as a standing hazard at §1.4 and D-55 — then records 7.1 and 8.1 without a word. If they are the same items, extract material from the towel and screwdriver survives, which is a first-order acquisition fact; if they are not, the collision is a live trap for every downstream file. Either way the question must be on the page.

findings.claim_in_file: "The State established ATF's ISO 17025 accreditation, validated methodologies, and competency and twice-yearly proficiency testing."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Two elements are dropped. (1) The accreditation is to TWO standards: "an international set of standards called ISO 17025 for testing laboratories, and additionally, a DNA specific set of standards put forth by the FBI," and the process is described as voluntary, with an external third-party audit. (2) The State's rehabilitation concession is omitted entirely: "The methodologies used in this case have been accepted by courts across the country, correct?" — "Correct."
findings.why_it_matters: The file records the defence-favourable content of Oliver's examination in dense detail. Omitting the one sentence in which she endorsed general acceptance of her methods, and the fact that ATF's DNA section is accredited to FBI-issued standards, produces an audit trail that leans one way in a section explicitly labelled "The State's cross."

findings.claim_in_file: "...and framed the result neutrally: 'It's reasonable to assume that anyone living in the household could have contributed to DNA on an object found in that household.'" The §3.4 ⚠ then refers to "that household-transfer explanation."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: That answer was given in response to a specific hypothetical counsel put to her — that if Lance Twiggs lived in the residence, came into contact with Tyler Robinson, and then touched a button on the Dremel, "you'd expect Mr. Robinson and Mr. Twiggs's DNA to be on there. Right? Or you could." She did not adopt the hypothetical. She substituted a general possibility statement.
findings.why_it_matters: Calling it "that household-transfer explanation" upgrades a declined hypothetical into a witness's offered account, and it is the phrase §3.4's Q-50 note then reasons from ("whether that household-transfer explanation reaches the towel and the screwdriver"). Since Q-50 is human-gated and concerns a living person testifying under use immunity, the provenance of the phrase should be exact.

findings.claim_in_file: §3.4 is titled "Consumption, and the elimination samples" and records the consumed and retained lists and the NRC 1996 rationale.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Three consumption facts are omitted, all of which the file records for Bakker at §2.8: (1) ATF's protocol — "we request permission to consume from the agent. We request that they reach out to an attorney if one is assigned... we will not begin any work on the case until we've received that permission to consume"; (2) she identified the permission email in her case notes (Oliver Three, p. 15); (3) she received the case on September 12, 2025, refreshed from Oliver Three p. 3, after counsel put "around September 11th." grep "permission to consume" and "September 12" over CR-E06 → 0 each.
findings.why_it_matters: §2.8 records the parallel Bakker fact ("She requested and received permission for destructive testing before receiving any samples"), so the asymmetry is visible on the page. The 2025-09-12 date is also the only calendar anchor Oliver gave, and the file assigns her none.

findings.claim_in_file: The firearm locations are listed as "stock and grips; butt plate; trigger and trigger guard; bolt; fore-end; barrel; the optical accessory; the protected underside of the receiver after disassembly; one .30-06 cartridge case; and two .30-06 cartridges."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Three of the items carry the qualifier "with possible ridge detail/smudging" (trigger and trigger guard; bolt; barrel), and the optical-accessory item is not "the optical accessory" but "the swabs of possible ridge detail/smudging on the optical accessory." The third cartridge is transcribed "the swabs of one 30-06 six cartridge" — a garble the file silently resolves to a second cartridge without listing it at §1.4.
findings.why_it_matters: "Possible ridge detail/smudging" identifies these as latent-print-associated swabs, which bears on where and how the material was collected and on the file's own point that Oliver did not do the swabbing. The unlisted garble is the only place in the block where the file resolves an ambiguous number without recording that it did so.

findings.claim_in_file: D-55(b): "the same FBI report is 'State's', 'People's' and 'plaintiff's' Exhibit 31 within Day 2." The Day-5 instance is not recorded.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Oliver's firearm report is called "State's Exhibit 30", "Plaintiff's Exhibit 30" and "Plaintiff's 30" by the same defence counsel within Day 5, and "exhibit number 30" by the prosecutor — inside the same day as the Baker-30 / State's-30 collision the file does record.
findings.why_it_matters: D-55 is the entry that instructs "No file may write a bare 'Exhibit 30' or 'Exhibit 31'". A second, independent instance of the party-prefix instability occurring on Day 5 strengthens the entry and shows the defect is not confined to Day 2.

findings.claim_in_file: "Entirely consumed: items 1.4, 1.6, 1.9, 1.10, 1.12, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1 and 5.1. Extracts retained (swabs consumed, liquid remaining): 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.5, 1.7, 1.8, 1.13, 7.1 and 8.1." Both lists are presented identically.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The two lists have different evidentiary provenance. The consumed list was read aloud by the WITNESS from her report ("It would be exhibits 1.4, 1.6..."). The retained list was read by COUNSEL as a compound question and confirmed only by "Correct."
findings.why_it_matters: The file's own sourcing rule distinguishes what a witness said from what counsel said and a witness assented to. The retained list is the one that contains items 7.1 and 8.1, so its provenance is load-bearing.

findings.claim_in_file: "The only likelihood ratio ever calculated for the elimination donor alone was 1" / "THE ONLY LIKELIHOOD RATIO EVER RUN ON THAT PRESUPPOSITION WAS 1." Stated flatly.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The exclusivity rests on a hedged answer, not a categorical one: "at that time, I believe I ran statistics with just Twiggs comparing that individual to the sample. If I may refer. I think that was the only additional." The LR value itself and the "uninformative" classification are categorical and I confirmed both; the word "only" is not.
findings.locator: day2.txt lines 7626–7633 ("I believe... I think that was the only additional"); 8093 and 8109 (the value and the classification)
findings.why_it_matters: This is the file's second headline result. The verified core — one Twiggs-alone STRmix run on item 7-1, dated 2025-09-15, LR = 1, classified uninformative, below the floor of 2 — survives intact; only the exclusivity claim outruns the witness's own hedge, and it should be marked as her recollection rather than as a fact about the case file.

confirmations.claim: ATTACK POINT (a) CONFIRMED — both headline figures place Lance Twiggs in BOTH competing propositions. Verbatim: item 7-1 is "1.7 octillion times more likely if Twiggs and T. Robinson are contributors than if Twiggs and an unknown, unrelated person are contributors"; item 8-1 is "30 quintillion times more likely if Twiggs and T. Robinson are contributors, than if Twiggs and an unknown, unrelated person are contributors." Both were read from State's Exhibit 31 by Sgt. Faumuina. Finding 5.1 and D-53 stand as written.

ATTACK POINT (b) CONFIRMED as to the value and the classification. "The likelihood ratio was one" — "Correct. It would fall under an uninformative" — and later "Based on the STRmix run, it was uninformative, but I did use my own knowledge and training to determine that I was going to utilize him as an assumed contributor." The floor of 2 for even limited support is also confirmed: "you need to reach a likelihood ratio of two in order to get even limited support for an inclusion, correct?" — "Correct, yes."

§2.2's exhibit and item detail CONFIRMED, including the item designation I expected to fail. The Twiggs-alone run is defence exhibit "Baker 38, page 39 through 44", admitted over a State relevance objection; and counsel put on the record, confirmed by the witness, "this is the STRmix unit dated September 15th and it relates to item 7-1, correct?" — "That is correct, yes." Inputs as the file states: two contributors assumed.

ATTACK POINT (c) — §5.3's substance survives. I ran tsearch.py /without (assuming|Twiggs)|unconditioned|if you had not assumed|not used him as an elimination/ over day2.txt (method self-validated against its known positive): 0 hits. No unconditioned Robinson likelihood ratio appears on this record, and the defence's attack was on the propriety of the assumption, not its magnitude. Only the phrase "was ever computed" overreaches (reported as a finding).

§3.4's flagged consumption point CONFIRMED and correct: item 2.1 appears on the entirely-consumed list AND is one of the two items in calculation number seven carrying an at-least-one-trillion likelihood ratio. The other item in that group, 1.13, and the calculation-3 item, 1.3, are both on the retained-extracts list.

Both trillion-order quotations in §3.2 are verbatim-exact, including the asymmetry the file preserves: calculation 3 reads "...than if it originated from four unrelated individuals" (not "four unknown unrelated"). Calculation 7's grouping rationale is also exact — same magnitude, two-person mixtures, and expressly "not that they were tested together."

Every bullet in §3.3 verified against the transcript: trigger and trigger guard swabbed together so "I wouldn't be able to say where the DNA came from"; degradation in 1.3 and the major profile carrying the most ("There was... Yes"); at least four contributors, could be five/six/seven, minor unsuitable for comparison "due to that complexity"; she did not perform the swabbing; item 1.1 a mixture of four individuals with two major contributors; no way of knowing when or how DNA was deposited; major/minor as quantity not activity; paragraph E carrying the same limitations including no source attribution.

Every bullet in §3.1 verified: the three unqualified activity disclaimers; "would not be scientifically defensible" for a "Robinson's DNA is found on this item" headline; "With forensic evidence, it's impossible to state with 100% certainty anything"; the five ATF conclusions including "uninformative"; no verbal scale; the one-trillion cap with her own rationale; her refusal to adopt the NIST rationale for the cap; the DOJ ULTR sentence in all three reports; her refusal to call the NIST publication a guidance document ("NIST is not a regulatory body for DNA testing"); and all evidence samples being mixtures, "sometimes four and five people."

§1.3's transcript lacuna CONFIRMED with exact metrics: a defence turn timestamped 01:15:51 is followed by an answering "Correct" timestamped 01:19:42 — 3 min 51 s — and the intervening text reads as a splice ("where the state read paragraph D, admitted paragraph F" appears mid-turn with no preceding question). It does fall at the inclusion-assent point.

Two §1.2 label failures CONFIRMED in my block: the oath administered TO Oliver carries her own name as speaker; and the answer "It's possible" to the ATF SOP four-person-mixture question carries the label "Ms. Visser", who is defence counsel (she later makes the record on Mr. Robinson's election not to testify). Content wins in both cases.

§1.4's exhibit-30 collision CONFIRMED as live within Oliver's examination: "Baker Exhibit 30" / "Baker-30" is the NIST publication Forensic DNA Interpretation and Human Factors, and "State's Exhibit 30" is Oliver's firearm DNA report — both handled within about thirty minutes of transcript.

§3.5's cross-day scoped null CONFIRMED by independent re-run. tsearch.py /iso ?allele/ (method self-validated): day1 0, day2 3, day3 0, day4 0, day5 3. "Isoallele" does appear in only two of the five days.
confirmations.locator: tsearch.py run over all five transcripts, 2026-08-01

confirmations.claim: The examination posture in §3 CONFIRMED: Oliver was called by the DEFENCE ("Mr. Burt, you may call your next witness" — "Call Ms. Oliver"), examined on direct by defence counsel, cross-examined by the State (the court: "if Mr. McBride, your cross is limited"), and re-examined by the defence. §3.2 and §3.3 are correctly labelled.

LIVING-PERSONS FRAMING — the Oliver block holds. Nothing in §3 states that anyone's DNA "was found on" anything; every elimination-donor result is rendered as "support for inclusion"; the ⚠ recording that the witness corrected counsel's "you found his DNA" is faithful in substance; Q-50 is expressly recorded and not answered; and no address, contact or locating detail about any private individual appears. The two qualifications are reported above: the "with a likelihood ratio attached" phrasing, and the upgrading of a declined hypothetical to "that household-transfer explanation." Neither reads as an accusation against Lance Twiggs, Matthew Robinson or Amber Robinson.

§3's biographical detail CONFIRMED: "Caitlin Oliver, O-L-I-V-E-R"; ATF DNA Section Chief "since January" with no year stated; "about nine years" with ATF; forensic biologist in September 2025. (One detail omitted by the file and non-material: before ATF she was a DNA analyst and DNA quality manager at the Jefferson Parish Sheriff's Office, New Orleans.)

output.scope_note:
WHAT I DID. I built an independent account of day5.txt 1380–2180 (Oliver — DNA persistence and degradation, elimination samples, report "157", the NGS line, the allele chart, isoalleles and the three objections, the exclusion-rule answer, the likelihood-ratio/number-of-contributors exchange, the NIST Mixture Study quotes, and the ATF SOP four-person-mixture exchange) BEFORE opening CR-E06. I then read day5.txt 640–1380 and 2178–2703 to place the block in Oliver's full examination, the State's cross, the defence re-examination, and the close of Day 5. Because attack points (a)–(c) name Bakker/Day-2 material, I also read day2.txt 7610–7770 and 8050–8210 and ran targeted validated searches over day2.txt. Only after all of that did I read CR-E06. Speakers were identified functionally (question vs answer, argument vs ruling), never from Rev labels. All searches used ./tsearch.py, self-validated against its known positive on each invocation; the case-sensitive NGS counts used grep -o.

WHAT I DID NOT DO. (1) I did not re-verify §2 (Bakker) other than the specific passages named in attack points (a)–(c) and §2.2's exhibit/item detail — §2.4 (the 3→2 NoC revision), §2.5 (PCAST), §2.6, §2.7, §2.8 (consumption, backpack), §2.9 and §2.10 are OUT OF SCOPE here and untested by me. (2) I did not verify §4 (the Exhibit 16 sanction, Exhibit 12.1, the adjournment) beyond what I read at day5.txt 2545–2703; the §4.1 findings-of-fact detail and the §4.2 timestamp analysis were not tested. (3) I did not re-verify §6's scoped nulls other than the isoallele null, the day2 unconditioned-LR null, and the /70% of four/ null I ran myself. (4) I did not verify §7's register-ceiling claim (D-52 highest assignment) or the D-56/D-57/D-58 entries. (5) I did not open any exhibit — like the file, everything here is a transcript account of documents no one in this library has read. (6) I checked the §1.2 "Mr. McBride = prosecutor AND media counsel" row only far enough to see it is not contradicted in my block; I did not test it, and it, not the Grunander row, is what finding 5.7 principally rests on. (7) Rev renderings only, not the certified transcript.

DIRECTIONALITY CHECK. Of the twenty findings, six run toward the State (the omitted "accepted by courts across the country" concession, the omitted substantive exclusion/dropout answer, the omitted "number matching" refusal, the §3.5 foreclosure overstatement, the §5.2 "only" over-assertion, and the §3.4 "likelihood ratio attached" overstatement) and five run against it (the omitted contamination rationale, the omitted "less than one in a trillion" figures, the omitted ATF SOP 70% passage, the omitted NGS answers, and the §5.3 unscoped world-claim). The file's Oliver sections are not systematically slanted; they are systematically INCOMPLETE — roughly a third of the block's substantive testimony, including the only overruled objection in the examination, does not appear in CR-E06 at all. The quotations that ARE in the file are accurate: every one of the roughly thirty I checked in §3.1–§3.4 verified verbatim or in faithful substance, and the two attack points that could have destroyed the headline findings (a and b) both survived. This reproduces the pattern the prior cycle recorded: the quotation pass confirms almost everything and the completeness pass finds the damage.

task: Q-58 VERIFICATION OF CR-E06, block 4 of 6: Oliver — the pre-testimony colloquy and early d

findings.claim_in_file: "The only likelihood ratio ever calculated for the elimination donor alone was 1 — 'uninformative,' below the threshold of 2 for even limited support" (§5.2, Confidence: High); "The only likelihood ratio ever run on him alone was 1" (D-53); "THE ONLY LIKELIHOOD RATIO EVER RUN ON THAT PRESUPPOSITION WAS 1" (headline #2).
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The quotes themselves are exact (day2, 07:20:59 "The likelihood ratio was one"; 07:21:08 "Correct. It would fall under an uninformative"), and the run was scoped to item 7-1. But the unbounded word "ever" is contradicted by the file's own §3.4. Oliver testified to "support for inclusion of Lance Twiggs on swabs of buttons of a Dremel tool" and again on "other areas of the Dremel tool" (day5.txt:1540, 1556). "Support for inclusion" is the TOP of her lab's five conclusions (day5.txt:827), she testified "we report the likelihood ratio and either support or support for inclusion or support for exclusion" (day5.txt:843), and as to the parallel Matthew Robinson conclusion she said "there would have been a likelihood ratio statistic calculated and to go along with that" (day5.txt:1528). ATF therefore ran likelihood ratios comparing Twiggs alone to multiple Dremel samples, and they did not come back at 1 or uninformative.
findings.why_it_matters: A High-confidence finding and a register entry both assert a global negative that the same file refutes two sections later. Anyone citing D-53 downstream would state that no informative statistic on this person exists, when the file itself records two. The claim is sound only if scoped: "the only likelihood ratio Bakker ran on Twiggs alone, against item 7-1, was 1." Left unscoped it is also a living-persons risk in the opposite direction — it understates results involving a person who is not accused.

findings.claim_in_file: "No alternative, unconditioned likelihood ratio for Robinson was ever computed, offered, or even requested anywhere in Bakker's testimony… Confidence: High that the record is silent on the consequence."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The record is not silent on the consequence. Bakker: "if I change the number of contributors to two, based on the studies and based on my own experience, it doesn't change the likelihood ratio of that major contributor by much." Burt: "But it does change it, correct?" Bakker: "Yes." (day2 06:10:30–06:10:38). Oliver, on the same question: "does the final likelihood ratio depend on the number of contributors you assume?" — "No, it does not." — "It has no effect, whatsoever?" — "It can have an effect. It's possible." (day5.txt:1984–1996), and earlier "It's not necessarily directly correlated with the number of contributors" (day5.txt:1964). The file's own §2.4 already carries the Bakker half.
findings.why_it_matters: §5.3 is the file's flagship over-hedge guard, graded High, and it is internally inconsistent with §2.4 of the same file. The defensible narrow claim is that no unconditioned ratio was computed so the MAGNITUDE of any effect is unquantified — not that the record is silent. As written it under-credits the State (both analysts gave testimony bearing on the consequence) while resting a High grade on a state of the record that does not obtain.

findings.claim_in_file: The file's declared read is "day5.txt lines 600–2703 (Oliver's direct, State's cross, defence redirect, excusal, and the close of the hearing)" (§1.1). Nothing from lines 600–643 appears anywhere in the file.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Lines 600–623 are the State's pre-testimony scope statement — the largest single speech in the block. It opens by quoting the court back to itself ("Sometimes you need to take time to save time"), states "a little over five hours" of defence witnesses so far, announces "a likely forthcoming standing objection" if testimony "exceeds the scope of the preliminary hearing, gets into areas of a 702 hearing," and cites six Utah authorities with quotations: State v. Schmidt, State v. Pledger (Utah 1995), State v. Hester (Utah Ct. App. 2000), State v. Virgin (Utah 2006), State v. Droesbeke (Utah Ct. App. 2010) and State v. Lopez (Utah 2020). It closes: "Your Honor has heard four days of testimony now. The evidence is overwhelming. It's devastating."
findings.why_it_matters: §3.5 reports that the State objected on relevance and the court sustained, without the announced framework those rulings rest on — and the State expressly incorporated this speech when objecting during Oliver's testimony: "based on Mr. Grunander's argument, I would invoke his argument here and the case law that he referenced" (day5.txt:1840). §8.8 also asks the library to verify case citations while omitting six Day 5 citations. A prosecutor's on-record characterisation of the whole case as "overwhelming… devastating" is recording-layer material a claim-inventory file should carry.

findings.claim_in_file: The file records counsel's stated purpose for calling Oliver but nothing of the exchange that immediately precedes it.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Defence counsel responded that a hearing date had been set for the court to rule on objections precisely "so that we wouldn't have to fly witnesses out from the East Coast if there was going to be a standing objection"; that before that hearing "the state contacted us after they had participated in interviews of Ms. Oliver and the other experts and indicated to us and we indicated to the court that there was going to be no standing objection to the testimony of these witnesses"; and therefore "if he's lodging a standing objection now, I think he's waived it or he should be stopped [estopped] from asserting it." He added he hoped to finish "by noon, direct and cross."
findings.why_it_matters: Three separate things are lost: (i) the procedural posture behind every objection the file does report in §3.5; (ii) the fact that the State interviewed Oliver — and "the other experts," plural — before she testified, which bears on the file's framing of both analysts as defence witnesses (headline #3); (iii) an unresolved waiver/estoppel question on the record. "Stopped" is also an unflagged garble of "estopped" belonging in §1.4.

findings.claim_in_file: §3.5 ends the direct at the isoallele rulings and §3.3 picks up at the redirect. The ~6 minutes between are absent.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: That span contains: (i) Oliver's express agreement with the NIST Mixture Study proposition that "A likelihood ratio numeric value is not a measurement of the physical quantity… Rather, it is a ratio of probabilities in the opinion of the expert assessing the likelihood ratio and is dependent on the specific propositions used to formulate it and also on the individual making the assessment" — "Correct. Yes, I agree"; (ii) the NoC/LR-dependence exchange ("No, it does not" / "It can have an effect"); (iii) her explanation that an LR "could be a low number and be a single-source sample. It could be a high number and be a four-person mixture"; (iv) the "at least five contributors" (1.2) and "at least four contributors" (1.1) report language and her concession that "at least" signals it could be more; (v) the ATF SOP p.83 figure that "approximately 70% of four-person mixtures present as two- or three-person mixtures," which she twice answered only as "It's possible."
findings.why_it_matters: Item (i) is the single most on-point corroboration of the file's own headline #1 — that a likelihood ratio is determined by the propositions chosen — and it comes from the OTHER analyst, at a different laboratory, on express agreement. The file builds its lead finding without it. Items (ii) and (v) bear directly on §5.3 and D-54. §8.3 already lists "ATF DNA SOP page 83" as an acquisition target while never stating what was read from it.

findings.target_section: §3.5 (the court's rulings on the State's objections)
findings.claim_in_file: "The State objected on relevance to a probable-cause hearing; the court SUSTAINED, twice, and sustained a third question on the ground that it did not tie to the witness's firsthand knowledge."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: There was a fourth State objection during Oliver's direct, to the SOP/70% line, and the court OVERRULED it: "I'll allow this question… So, I'll overrule the objection. She may review the material, and the… question can be rephrased." Defence counsel's successful response was "he's implying it's going to be an extended discussion. I have one question which she wants to look at her manual to make sure it's in there, and then I'm done."
findings.why_it_matters: The file records three sustains and no overrule. That is a one-directional record of the court's rulings on a single witness — the exact pattern the project's objectivity mechanics name as a bias signal. It also matters substantively: the one line the court permitted is the one the file omits.

findings.target_section: §2.10 / §6 (exhibit irregularities; scoped null on ULTR admission)
findings.claim_in_file: §2.10 flags as an irregularity that on Day 2 "The DOJ ULTR probabilistic-genotyping policy (defence Tab 8) was displayed TO THE WITNESS ONLY and NEVER admitted… Two substantive policy provisions were read into the record from an unadmitted document." §6's scoped null on ULTR admission is scoped to Bakker's block.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The same thing happened again on Day 5, and the file's own read range covers it. "Could you go now to Exhibit Oliver Four for the witness only? Not admitted yet" — the DOJ ULTR document — after which FOUR provisions were read into the record from it (mandatory verbal scale if one is used; no infallibility/zero error rate; no absolute identification or source attribution from a likelihood ratio of any magnitude; no "reasonable degree of scientific certainty"). The NIST publication was likewise "Baker Exhibit 30, page one, for the witness only"; her case record was "Oliver Three for the witness only" including "page 15 of those case notes… Again, for the witness only"; and the allele chart was "154, please, for the witness only." Only "Oliver 157, which has been admitted" and State's Exhibit 30 ("which is in evidence") are stated to be in evidence.
findings.why_it_matters: The file treats the Day 2 instance as a flaggable irregularity and misses the Day 5 recurrence, so the pattern — the defence's entire limitations examination at both laboratories conducted from documents shown to the witness only — is never stated. It also interacts with §4.1: with the morning's sanction barring exhibit display, substantive federal policy text was read aloud from documents that neither the public nor the exhibit record received. §6's null should be re-scoped or a Day 5 companion added.

findings.claim_in_file: "⚠ 'State v. Drozbeck' (Day 2) does not resolve to a verifiable case name and must not be cited from this transcript" (§1.4); repeated at §8.8.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Day 2 renders it "State v. Drozbeck" in a string cite (07:13:03). Day 5, at line 619 — inside the file's own declared read range — renders the same case as "State v. Droesbeke case, which is a Utah Court of Appeals case 2010," with the same holding the Day 2 objection invoked ("wholly lacking and incapable of creating a reasonable inference"). Validated search: /Droesbeke|Drozbeck|Drosbeck/ via ./tsearch.py across day1–day5 returns exactly 2 hits, one per day, both opened.
findings.why_it_matters: The caveat is stated too strongly and the disambiguating orthography, court and year sat unread inside the block the file says it read end to end. The correct entry is that Day 2's "Drozbeck" is a garble of Day 5's "Droesbeke," a 2010 Utah Court of Appeals case — still "— (checkable)" against a reporter, but no longer unresolvable. This is a completeness-pass failure of exactly the type the file's own §9.2 anticipates.

findings.claim_in_file: Table row: "'Chad Grunander' (a prosecutor)" is really "Defence co-counsel, asking that a record be made with the livestream operators."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The turn is: "Judge, I might simply add, given the court's ruling this morning with respect to displaying exhibits, we may want to make a record with the live-streaming folks here that it's not going to be published" (day5.txt:2613–2616). No basis for reassignment is stated. The content fits the State at least as well as the defence: the State is the proponent of Exhibit 12.1 and had just moved to publish it in the courtroom. And the label is independently corroborated as the prosecutor on the same day and in this very block — the judge asks "And to the state?" and the answer comes under "Chad Grunander" (day5.txt:735–739), as does the State's scope statement at 01:07:07 after the judge says "Yes, Mr. Grunander."
findings.why_it_matters: The file's own rule is "name a person only with a stated basis… WHERE LABEL AND CONTENT DISAGREE, CONTENT WINS." Here content does not disagree and no basis is given, so the row inverts the rule and manufactures a hazard instance. §5.7 and the promoted library-wide caveat rest partly on this table; the McBride row carries them on its own, but a fabricated instance in a table promoted library-wide is a defect that propagates.

findings.claim_in_file: The sanction is stated from the ruling text plus the monitor colloquy; §4.1 asserts "The sanction's practical effect went well beyond its words, and this is not visible from the ruling text."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Minutes into Oliver's direct the court interrupted to put the sanction's scope on the record: a question had arisen "whether audio could be transmitted, and my ruling covered the video display of any exhibits"; "the audio of your portion discussing evidence… is going to be captured by the camera and displayed, but not any exhibits displayed." Defence, State and media each confirmed that understanding on the record. The court added that "the parties are responsible to monitor their monitors" and that although the camera is "directed not to focus on the monitors… inevitable capture may occur."
findings.why_it_matters: This is the operative scope clarification of the sanction, obtained from all three parties, and it is the reason the Exhibit 12.1 "livestream to audio only" mechanic at §4.2 was available at all. §4.1 claims the sanction's effect is not visible from the ruling text while omitting the on-record clarification of that very effect.

findings.claim_in_file: §3.1 records "Her lab uses NO verbal qualifier scale — no 'strong,' no 'very strong.'" §5.4 finds the two analysts agreed "in identical terms." No finding records where they diverge.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The divergence was elicited expressly against the FBI. Counsel: "We've had a prior witness testify that, from the FBI testified that they use a scale and they characterize the support along the lines of strong…" Oliver: "our laboratory doesn't use a verbal scale due to the fact that they add subjective words to the front of this word support. It is our stance that the likelihood ratio statistic, the number stands on its own." Separately, ATF caps reporting at one trillion — "The actual number could be a lot higher. It could be quintillion, octillion" — while the two FBI figures the file headlines are 1.7 octillion and 30 quintillion, uncapped.
findings.why_it_matters: The file synthesises two laboratories and finds only agreement. The State's ATF analyst gave a reasoned, on-record criticism of exactly the verbal-scale practice §2.2 relies on for the "uninformative"/"limited support"/"very strong" bands that carry D-53 — and the two labs' reporting conventions make a trillion-order ATF figure and an octillion-order FBI figure non-comparable magnitudes. Both belong in §5 alongside §5.4, and the second belongs in D-53.

findings.claim_in_file: "She was then asked whether any investigator told her the towel did not come from the home but was found in a bush at the university. She answered: 'I was aware of that, yes.' … 'That is correct. It was found outside of a home. But again…'"
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The question hidden by the ellipsis is the strongest concession in the exchange: "So you knew that that towel was not found in a place where you would inspect [expect] Mr. Twiggs' DNA to be present?" — "That is correct. It was found outside of a home." Also omitted is her preceding hedge on the basis for the designation: "I don't recall exactly if it was a situation where a particular towel was known to have been in that house. I don't remember that exactly. But in talking to the investigators… it was important to assume potentially Mr. Twiggs was present."
findings.why_it_matters: An ellipsis that conceals which question an answer answers is the selective-quotation hazard operating inside the file rather than on it. Here the elision runs against the file's own headline #1 — the concession that the item was not found where the assumed contributor's DNA would be expected is the sharpest support for D-53 that the record contains, and the omitted hedge weakens the investigator-instruction basis §5.2 rests on. Both directions of the ledger lose.

findings.claim_in_file: "Whether that household-transfer explanation reaches the towel and the screwdriver — which were recovered away from the household… — bears on a living person who is not accused and who testified under use immunity. The question is recorded. It is not answered."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: As framed, the question presupposes that this person's DNA is on the towel and screwdriver and therefore needs explaining. The file's own headline #1 says the opposite about the statistic: it "never tests whether Twiggs is present. It presupposes it," and the only STRmix run on him alone returned 1/uninformative. The only record basis for his presence is Bakker's visual comparison — "When I compared him to that data, I did see his DNA present" — which the file quotes at §2.2 but does not connect here.
findings.locator: file §3.4 vs file headline #1 and §2.2; day2 07:21:25
findings.why_it_matters: An open question about a living person under use immunity is framed on a premise the same file says was never established by the statistic. Either the premise needs its stated basis attached (Bakker's visual determination, expressly not a statistical one) or the presupposition needs flagging. As written, a reader who takes Q-50 at face value has been handed an unstated assumption about a person who is not accused of anything — which is the precise failure mode the living-persons header exists to prevent.

findings.claim_in_file: §3.4 lists what was consumed and retained and reaches the ⚠ on item 2.1, but records no date for Oliver's assignment and nothing about her consumption-permission procedure. Compare §2.8, which does record Bakker's: "She requested and received permission for destructive testing before receiving any samples."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Two things are on the record. Dates: counsel asked "do you recall that around September 11th, you received a request to do some DNA work at the request of the state of Utah?" — "Yes"; refreshed from Oliver Three p.3 she gave "September 12th, 2025" as receipt, and confirmed "Yes, it is" that this was when she first started work. Consent: "it's standard procedure at our laboratory that when we receive a case, we request permission to consume from the agent. We request that they reach out to an attorney if one is assigned. And in this case, we will not begin any work on the case until we've received that permission to consume," documented by an email at case-notes p.15.
findings.why_it_matters: The library dates everything, and D-54 turns on 2025-09-12/13 in Bakker's work; an ATF receipt date of 2025-09-12 with a request "around September 11th" is directly comparable and the mild tension between the two is checkable. Omitting the consent procedure is also one-directional: §3.4's consumption material reads as a defence point, and the record contains a documented consent process that expressly contemplates defence counsel — the counter-weight the objectivity mechanics require be logged.

findings.claim_in_file: "An apparent ~3 min 51 s untranscribed span sits inside Oliver's direct (day5.txt 708–715)… Content is missing, not merely compressed. ⚠ It falls at the point of the only Tyler-Robinson inclusion assent in the whole direct."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The characterisation is correct and well-founded — but the surviving fragment shows what the lacuna swallowed and the file does not say so. The spliced turn reads: "Could we display State's Exhibit 30, which is in evidence? For instance, the next sample down, 1.2, where the state read paragraph D, admitted paragraph F, you state in F, based on this calculation, there is evidentiary support for the inclusion of Tyler Robinson, correct? As a possible contributor." "The next sample down" presupposes an unrecorded prior sample; "where the state read paragraph D, admitted paragraph F" presupposes an unrecorded exposition of the report's paragraph lettering.
findings.why_it_matters: The paragraph D / paragraph F distinction is the concrete instantiation of the charge the file quotes at §3 — that the State "selectively read into the record a portion of those reports." The file records the general accusation and loses the only surviving evidence of its specific content. It also supplies the affirmative basis for §1.3's own "content is missing, not merely compressed," which is currently asserted without it.

findings.claim_in_file: "both analysts said so expressly and repeatedly, and one of them said a headline of that form 'would not be scientifically defensible.'"
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The witness did not say those words. Defence counsel put them: "And that would not be scientifically defensible, would it?" — and she answered "Correct." §3.1 and the revision log both render it correctly as agreement; only the header says "said."
findings.why_it_matters: Counsel's words inside quotation marks attributed to a witness is the recording-layer error the prime directive forbids, and it sits in the one paragraph most likely to be read and quoted onward. The fix is one word: "agreed."

findings.claim_in_file: "Oliver, three times and never qualified" / "⚠ Three times, never qualified" followed by three quotations.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The three quoted instances are verbatim and correctly located. There is at least a fourth, equally unqualified: "So, this is what you were stating about calling a major contributor. It doesn't speak to the activity that led to the DNA deposition," plus assents at 01:45:17 ("you can't make any assessment of how or when DNA got deposited. Correct?" — "Correct") and on redirect at 02:20:23.
findings.why_it_matters: A count is a checkable claim and this one is low. It errs safe, but the project's own rule is that an unwarranted hedge is as reportable as an unwarranted assertion, and a downstream file relying on "three times" would understate the most consistent thing in the DNA record.

findings.claim_in_file: "Both are called 'Exhibit 30' within minutes of each other. Never write a bare 'Exhibit 30' — or a bare 'Exhibit 31,' which appears as State's, People's and plaintiff's within Day 2 alone." D-55(a) is confined to the NIST/report collision; the party-designation drift is presented as a Day 2, Exhibit 31 phenomenon.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Oliver's report also drifts across party designations on Day 5 itself: "State's Exhibit 30, which is in evidence" (01:15:51), bare "Exhibit 30, page eight" (01:31:08), "Let's talk about the samples in Plaintiff's Exhibit 30" (01:32:32), and on redirect "It's Exhibit 30. Plaintiff's 30. Right?" (02:20:55). Day 5 also runs two parallel defence exhibit series, "Baker N" and "Oliver N," simultaneously.
findings.why_it_matters: D-55's rule is right; its evidence is thinner than the record supports. The Day 5 instances show the same designator drifting across three party names within a single witness's examination — a stronger case than the cross-day Exhibit 31 example, and it belongs in the entry.

findings.claim_in_file: "the State's Exhibit 16 sanction" (§1.1); "State's Exhibit 24 was displayed on the monitor visible to the media camera; State's Exhibit 16 was displayed on ALL monitors…" (§4.1).
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The court's findings say both bare: "Exhibit 24 was displayed on the monitor visible to the media camera. Exhibit 16 was displayed on all monitors…" Validated search: /State's Exhibit 16|State's Exhibit 24|Exhibit 24/ over day5.txt via ./tsearch.py returns exactly 1 hit — this passage. No Day 5 text assigns either exhibit to a party. ("State's Exhibit 12.1" is by contrast said in terms at 02:24:17 and 02:27:55, and the file is right to use it.)
findings.why_it_matters: The file adds party designations the record does not supply, in the same document that promulgates D-55's rule against exactly this. Either source the designation from Day 4 or write it bare.

findings.claim_in_file: "the towel and the screwdriver — which were recovered away from the household (the towel in a wooded area, the screwdriver on the roof)"
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The screwdriver is right and is established: "Item 8, Screwdriver from perch" and "is that the screwdriver that you described that was collected from the rooftop?" — "Yes." The towel is not: the record phrase is "found in a bush out at the university" and "It was found outside of a home" — which the file itself quotes correctly at §2.3. "Wooded area" is Agent Hull's phrase for a different subject (the route across Campus Drive).
findings.why_it_matters: The conclusion is unaffected — both descriptions place it away from the household — but the drift is inside the one paragraph concerning a living person under use immunity, and it imports a phrase from an unrelated witness's narrative. Precision costs nothing here.

findings.claim_in_file: The garble list is drawn almost entirely from Day 2; no Day 5 garble is listed.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Oliver's summary of the ULTR is transcribed as: "It also says that we cannot state that our evidence is infallible, nor can we state that there is a inconclusive result." Counsel's very next question is "Shall not state that it's infallible or have a zero error rate, correct?" — "Correct." As rendered the witness states a proposition (that the lab may not report an inconclusive result) that neither counsel's follow-up nor any other part of the record supports. Day 5 also renders "the National NRC" (for National Research Council), "he should be stopped" (estopped), "please approach the electron" (lectern), and "one 30-06 six cartridge."
findings.why_it_matters: §1.4 is the file's trap list and D-57 exists precisely because a mis-rendered figure is a live trap for downstream quotation. "Nor can we state that there is a inconclusive result" is either an unrecorded substantive ULTR provision or an unflagged garble; the file resolves it neither way because it records the answer nowhere.

findings.claim_in_file: "the only Tyler-Robinson inclusion assent in the whole direct" (§1.3); "No alternative, unconditioned likelihood ratio for Robinson was ever computed, offered, or even requested anywhere in Bakker's testimony" (§5.3).
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Both are absence claims. I could not fault either on the merits — I read Burt's direct end to end and found no second Robinson-inclusion assent within it — but neither states a pattern, a day or a tool, and neither appears in §6, which is where the file otherwise disciplines exactly this move ("Each is a claim about a full-text search… run with ./tsearch.py").
findings.why_it_matters: Standing hazard 5: a search null is a claim about the search. The file holds itself to that standard eight times in §6 and drops it twice in the two places where the null carries a High-confidence finding. Either migrate them into §6 with their patterns or downgrade them to observations.

findings.claim_in_file: The table lists four Day 5 label failures and adds that victim's-family counsel appears as "Jeff Dyer" (9×), "Jeff Nyman" (1×) and "Jeffrey Neiman" — "three renderings, one speaker."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: A fifth Day 5 rendering is unrecorded: media counsel also appears as an unnamed "Speaker 1," three times in this block, each time immediately after the court turns to the media ("I'm not sure if the media needs to be heard" → "No, Your Honor"; "And to the media?" → "Yes, Your Honor. There might be concern about the actual monitors…"). Separately, "three renderings, one speaker" is asserted as established and then immediately followed by "Do not resolve any of these to a real person from Rev labels alone" — the record shows only that two speakers each self-identify as "Jeff" appearing "on behalf of the victim."
findings.why_it_matters: §1.2 is promoted to a library-wide caveat, so its inventory should be complete and its identity claims should meet the standard the same paragraph sets. The "one speaker" inference is not load-bearing anywhere in the file, so it can simply be softened.

findings.claim_in_file: "I don't know that I would call it a guidance document. NIST is not a regulatory body for DNA testing. It was a report that looked into forensic DNA reporting and specific human factors."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The sentence is truncated mid-clause and closed with a full stop. The witness said: "…specific human factors that could affect our testing. So, they may have had recommendations, but as far as them being a regulatory body that's issuing guidelines, I wouldn't state that."
findings.why_it_matters: Silent truncation without ellipsis, and the omitted tail is the strongest part of the refusal — the part that concedes NIST made recommendations while denying it regulates. The file is quoting this to demonstrate a point cutting against the party that called her; the full quotation makes the point better.

findings.claim_in_file: Title and §3: "Caitlin Oliver (spelled O-L-I-V-E-R), DNA Section Chief at ATF, in that role 'since January' (no year stated on the record); ~9 years with ATF; previously a forensic biologist, and a DNA analyst before ATF."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Accurate as far as it goes, and the "no year stated" flag is a good catch. Omitted: she was asked directly "Back in September of 2025, what were your duties and responsibilities?" and answered "I was a forensic biologist" — i.e. she was not Section Chief when she did this casework. Also omitted is the prior employer and the second prior role: "Jefferson Parish Sheriff's Office in New Orleans, Louisiana as a DNA analyst and a DNA quality manager."
findings.why_it_matters: The file identifies her throughout by her current title, including in the file title and §1.1. Without the September 2025 role, a reader infers section-chief seniority over the analysis itself. The quality-manager role and the named prior laboratory are also standard qualifications material — and §2.7/§6 make a point of Bakker's qualifications being elicited only on cross, so the comparison should be complete.

findings.claim_in_file: "one .30-06 cartridge case; and two .30-06 cartridges"
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: She read three separate entries: "The swabs of one 30-06 cartridge case, the swabs of one 30-06 cartridge and the swabs of one 30-06 six cartridge." The file merges the last two into "two cartridges," which is a reasonable reading but is an inference, and "one 30-06 six cartridge" is an unflagged garble.
findings.why_it_matters: These are separately numbered items (the consumed list runs 3.1, 4.1, 5.1), so merging two enumerated entries into a count obscures the item-to-designator mapping that §8.5 already flags as unresolved for the bolt swab.

confirmations.claim: Headline #1 / §5.1 / D-53 — CONFIRMED, and this is the file's strongest work. Both figures place Lance Twiggs in both competing propositions: item 7-1 "1.7 octillion times more likely if Twiggs and T. Robinson are contributors than if Twiggs and an unknown, unrelated person are contributors"; item 8-1 "30 quintillion times more likely if Twiggs and T. Robinson are contributors, than if Twiggs and an unknown, unrelated person are contributors." The presence of the elimination donor is on both sides of both ratios. §2.1's attribution is also right: both were read by Sgt. Faumuina from the report, not uttered by Bakker.
confirmations.locator: day2 05:10:57 and 05:11:41 (Faumuina reading Item 7.1 and Item 8.1)

confirmations.claim: §2.2's "2 is the floor for even 'limited support for an inclusion'" — CONFIRMED, and it does NOT depend on the garbled band table. The witness assented in terms: "So you need to reach a likelihood ratio of two in order to get even limited support for an inclusion, correct?" — "Correct, yes." My hypothesis that this number was contaminated by the transcription defect the file itself flags is disproved.

§2.2's ⚠ that the verbal scale "as transcribed" assigns "very strong support for inclusion" to two adjacent bands — CONFIRMED verbatim: "if I have a likelihood ratio that's greater than or equal to one million, I designate that as very strong support for inclusion. The next example, 10,000 to less than one million, I would say that's very strong support for inclusion and so forth."

§2.2's two quoted answers on the likelihood ratio of one — CONFIRMED verbatim: "The likelihood ratio was one" and "Correct. It would fall under an uninformative." So is §2.2's ⚠ that she answered only the second limb of the compound "not a contributor / not even of limited value" question: "Based on the STRmix run, it was uninformative, but I did use my own knowledge and training…"

§1.3's lacuna — CONFIRMED on every element. The line range 708–715 is exact; 01:15:51 → 01:19:42 is 3 min 51 s; and "content is missing, not merely compressed" is affirmatively supported, because the surviving fragment presupposes material that is not in the transcript ("the next sample down, 1.2" and "where the state read paragraph D, admitted paragraph F"). I also independently read Burt's whole direct and found no second Tyler-Robinson inclusion assent within it.

§1.2 speaker-label table, row 1 — CONFIRMED, and it is the strongest instance. The judge says "Thank you, Mr. McBride. To the media," and the next turn, still labelled "Mr. McBride," opens "Appreciate the opportunity to be here to speak on behalf of the media." It recurs later the same morning: "Turning to the state, and then to the media" → "Mr. McBride" (State, 54:45) → "To the media" → "Mr. McBride" (media, 56:29).
§1.2 row 2 — CONFIRMED. The oath ("Do you solemnly swear that the testimony you shall give…") carries the label "Caitlin Oliver," i.e. the witness being sworn, not the officer administering it.

§1.2 row 3 — CONFIRMED. "Ms. Visser" carries the witness's answer "It's possible" to counsel's SOP question; and Ms. Visser is independently established as defence counsel by content and by the court addressing her ("We have advised Mr. Robinson of his right to testify… Thank you, Ms. Visser").

§3's quotation of defence counsel's stated purpose for calling Oliver — CONFIRMED verbatim, word for word, including "through a non-expert," "selectively read into the record a portion of those reports" and "extremely misleading impression of the significance of that evidence." (Only "and that's it" is dropped from the tail.)

§3.4 consumption lists — CONFIRMED item-for-item, in order, with no transposition. Entirely consumed: 1.4, 1.6, 1.9, 1.10, 1.12, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1, 5.1 (from the witness's own mouth). Extracts retained: 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.5, 1.7, 1.8, 1.13, 7.1, 8.1 (read by counsel, assented "Correct"). The gloss "swabs consumed, liquid remaining" is also confirmed: "Does your report mean that you consume the swabs, but you have some liquid extract remaining as to those samples?" — "Correct."

§3.4's ⚠ that item 2.1 — one of the two items carrying a trillion-order likelihood ratio — is on the entirely-consumed list: CONFIRMED on both legs independently. 2.1 appears in the consumed list, and 2.1 is one of the two exhibits in calculation number seven. Its companion 1.13 is correctly on the retained list, so "one of the two" is exact.

§3.1's three activity-disclaimer quotations — all three CONFIRMED verbatim and correctly unqualified: "None of the testing that I performed could speak to activity or what activity led to the deposition of the DNA"; "That is true. DNA can't speak to the activity that led to the deposition of the DNA"; "Yes. Once again, I cannot speak to the activity."

§3.1's five ATF conclusion categories — CONFIRMED verbatim: "exclusion, limited support for exclusion, uninformative, limited support for inclusion, and support for inclusion," together with "We don't use a verbal scale at our laboratory."

§3.1's one-trillion cap quotation — CONFIRMED verbatim including "It could be quintillion, octillion" and the "has meaning to people" rationale; and §3.2's "capped floors" is confirmed by "We would not report a number higher than one trillion."

§3.1's ⚠ that she DECLINED to adopt the NIST rationale for the reporting cap — CONFIRMED: "I believe we chose our cap for the reason I stated," then "I'm not familiar with the paper that's referenced there, so I would have to familiarize myself before I said I… agreed or disagreed."

§3.1's ⚠ that she REFUSED the defence's framing of the NIST publication, logged as a point cutting against the party that called her — CONFIRMED, and correctly characterised. This is the file honouring "verify in both directions" on the record rather than in the abstract.
