The immediately preceding turn ties the 5%/95% figures to item seven ("Same question with regard to eight" follows). The file demonstrably read eight lines further on, because D-57 quotes the item-8 answer from that very exchange.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a negative claim about the record — a scoped-null-type assertion made with no stated search — and the record contradicts it in the very block the file cites for the neighbouring D-57 entry. Under hazard 5 and hazard 11 it is the highest-value class of error the file can contain, and it is the kind a quotation-only pass cannot catch.

findings.claim_in_file: §2.5 records only that "She agreed both samples had minor contributors below 20%: item 7 at 5%/95%, item 8 at 11%/89%," and that her rebuttal was "in this case it was also only a mixture of two individuals." §5.3 asserts the record is silent on consequence.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: On cross the witness placed Tyler Robinson with the MAJOR component in both items and Lance Twiggs with the minor: item 7 — "Twiggs' DNA profile aligned with the 5% contributor and Mr. Robinson's DNA profile aligned better with the 95% contributor"; item 8 — "Twiggs better aligned with that 11% contributor and Mr. Robinson better aligned with that 79% [sic, put as 89%] contributor."
findings.why_it_matters: PCAST's 20% criterion is about the MINOR contributor's interpretability. On this testimony the sub-20% fraction is the elimination donor's, not the defendant's — which is a far more direct answer to the defence's PCAST attack than the two-person rebuttal the file records, and it is the single most State-favourable fact in the block. Its absence makes the §2.5 analysis and the §5.3 over-hedge guard both run without it, and an audit trail that omits the strongest point for one side is itself a bias signal under the project's own rule.

findings.claim_in_file: "THE ONLY LIKELIHOOD RATIO EVER RUN ON THAT PRESUPPOSITION WAS 1" / "The only likelihood ratio ever calculated for the elimination donor alone was 1" / "The only likelihood ratio ever run on him alone was 1".
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The record establishes one such run, on one item. Counsel: "this is the STRmix unit dated September 15th and it relates to item 7-1, correct?" — "That is correct, yes." Inputs walked through are all item-7 ("You input sample 7A?" — "Correct"). The LR of 1 is read off "page 39 … Second page" of that report. The exhibit admitted was "Baker 38, pages 39 through 44" — six pages, of which only pp. 39–40 are described on the record; pp. 41–44 are never identified. Counsel's own framing keeps the two items separate: "despite this STRmix reading with a likelihood ratio of one, that Mr. Twiggs was a contributor to both item seven and item eight." Nothing establishes whether a Twiggs-alone ratio was or was not run on item 8-1. The file's own §6 scoped null supports a different proposition ("the only likelihood-ratio VALUE BAKKER HERSELF STATES on direct is one"), not this one.
findings.why_it_matters: A universal negative is asserted where the record carries a single-item positive, and it is carried into a headline, a finding and a register entry. Steelman for the file: she testified she does not routinely run STRmix on elimination samples (07:23:22), so one run is plausible — but that is an inference, not a verification act. The safe form is "the only likelihood ratio for the elimination donor in evidence was 1, computed on item 7-1."

findings.target_section: §2.6 final bullet, read against §9 residual item 8
findings.claim_in_file: §9.8: "Partial STR genotype data spoken in open court is **summarised, not reproduced**." §2.6 then reproduces it: "at **D16** Twiggs is 9,12 … at **D19S** he is 14,16 … at **THO1** he is 7, 9.3."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The exchanges are real (D16 "912"; D19S "1416"; THO "79.3"), but the file states three called genotypes for a named living private individual who testified under use immunity and is accused of nothing, in flat contradiction of its own residual-scope promise two sections later.
findings.why_it_matters: CLAUDE.md forbids identifying information about uninvolved parties even when the source publishes it, and genotype data is identifying information about a non-accused person. The internal contradiction also means a reader trusting §9 will not know §2.6 contains this. The analytic point (his types were not fully recovered from item 8) survives intact if the alleles are replaced with "one of his two called alleles was not recovered at each of three loci."

findings.claim_in_file: "**The court's admission ruling names the wrong exhibit.** … the judge's ruling then reads 'I'll admit into evidence under the previous statement as it relates to Baker 34.' **An exhibit-identity defect created by the record itself, not by the transcription.**" D-55 calls this "the serious one."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The judge's full words are: "All right. I'll admit into evidence under the previous statement as it relates to Baker 34. It may be published." There is a prior statement expressly relating to Baker 34 that the ruling can be incorporating: at 07:44:47 the court said "So I will admit Baker 34, but Mr. Burt, I'm going to limit you to … How much time do you need to address this?" — an admission plus a limit. On that reading "as it relates to Baker 34" modifies "the previous statement," and the court is admitting Baker 35 on the terms it set for Baker 34.
findings.why_it_matters: The project requires steelmanning before resolving, and this reading is at least as natural as the file's. The file states the adverse reading flatly, calls it a defect in the record rather than the transcription, and builds a register entry on it. It should be recorded as ambiguous on the face of the Rev rendering and resolvable only against the certified transcript.

findings.claim_in_file: "the admitted defence exhibits are Bakker 7, Baker 4 (pp. 365 and 128), Baker 38 and Baker 34 **only**."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Baker 35 (the isoallele chart) was moved into evidence and admitted: Burt "So I move this exhibit into evidence, Your Honor, and for publication"; after the numbering was corrected to 35 twice, McBride: "Same objection, Your Honor"; Judge: "I'll admit into evidence under the previous statement as it relates to Baker 34. It may be published." The file's own §2.10 describes this admission.
findings.why_it_matters: The bullet is presented as the product of a verification act ("every admission hit in Bakker's block opened") and closes with "only," so it will be read as an exhaustive list. It is not, and it contradicts the file's own §2.10. Whatever view is taken of the Baker 34/35 ambiguity, an exhibit was admitted at that moment and the list omits it.

findings.target_section: §2.5; §2.2; §5.3 — the defence redirect and the State's re-cross are entirely unrecorded
findings.claim_in_file: §2.5 is titled "The PCAST exchange — the defence's strongest line, and her answer" and records only the direct-examination PCAST material.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: After the State's cross, the defence conducted a five-minute redirect that the file does not cover at all: (i) two further PCAST passages read to her — on experience/judgment not establishing scientific validity, and on good professional practices not substituting for evidence of validity — which she expressly DISAGREED with ("I don't" / "I don't think I agree with that either"); (ii) "That name does not ring a bell. I don't know who that individual is" / "No, I do not" when asked about Eric Lander; (iii) her answer that "There was 31 laboratories that came together in response to the PCAS report and gave their validation data," and her assent that PCAST addressed and was "unpersuaded by those studies"; (iv) the 2004 DOJ Inspector General audit of the FBI DNA laboratory — the State's relevance objection was OVERRULED for a single question and she answered "No, I'm not" aware of it; (v) counsel's sharpest formulation of the Twiggs point, "The software told you there was no support there for including them and you ignored it and decided otherwise, correct?" and her denial, "I did not ignore it. Again, given the type of sample, it was an elimination sample…"; (vi) the State's re-cross on ground truth: "Your validation actually is a ground truth test in essence?" — "Yes."
findings.why_it_matters: This is roughly 150 lines of the block, containing material cutting both ways: her flat rejection of PCAST's core methodological claims and the 31-laboratory response help the State; not recognising Eric Lander and being unaware of the IG audit help the defence. Item (v) is the on-record answer to the file's most pointed process insinuation (§2.3's "the decision … is recorded as already settled"), and the file never pairs the insinuation with the denial.

findings.target_section: §2 ("Who she is" / the qualifications note) — the State's cross of Bakker
findings.claim_in_file: "her entire qualifications — degree, accreditation, the two-year training programme with oral and written boards and moot court, competency and proficiency testing — were elicited by the STATE on cross"; and "a DNA analyst there 'a little more than 10 years.'"
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The State's cross runs ~180 lines and its substance is nowhere recorded: B.S. in biology, Salisbury University; FBI contractor on the Federal Convicted Offender Program ~18 months; biologist in the DNA Casework Unit ~6 years doing the bench work; forensic examiner since 2015, assented to as "11 years"; ANAB accreditation, externally audited every four years against training records and SOPs; ≥8 hours annual continuing education; outside-vendor proficiency testing that "also tests the laboratory process"; mandatory technical AND administrative review of every case; validated tools and SOPs; STRmix developmentally validated in a peer-reviewed study and used in "approximately 120 laboratories"; and the closing anchor — "did you follow the protocols of your accredited lab?" / "did you in fact come to the conclusions described in Exhibit 31?" — "Yes, I did" to both.
findings.why_it_matters: §3.2 records the equivalent block for Oliver (ISO 17025, validated methodologies, twice-yearly proficiency testing). Recording it for one witness and not the other is the asymmetry the project treats as a bias signal. Separately, "a DNA analyst there a little more than 10 years" reads as total tenure; on this testimony it describes only her examiner tenure, with ~7½ further years at the FBI DNA unit before it — a downstream file could understate her experience by half.

findings.claim_in_file: "**No alternative, unconditioned likelihood ratio for Robinson was ever computed, offered, or even requested** anywhere in Bakker's testimony… **Confidence: High** that the record is silent on the consequence."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The silence is real (confirmed below) but its scope is not stated. The examination was under an express, escalating court-imposed time cap at exactly the point the topic would have been developed: "And Mr. Burt, we are at the 4:30 point"; "I'm going to allow the admission of this evidence, but I'm also going to set a limit of a limited number of questions. And we are now at 4:40"; "how much time do you need to address this?" — "about four to five minutes"; and the State's "I need to cross-examine this witness. She's got to leave town today. I would like 20 minutes." Redirect was likewise capped at "Five minutes," and the State's cross closed with "It's 5:00. I'm going to wrap up."
findings.why_it_matters: The project's rule is that absence of evidence is a finding WITH A SCOPE. Silence produced under a court-imposed cap and repeated sustained relevance objections carries different weight from silence in an unconstrained examination. The over-hedge guard is right to exist; it is under-scoped as written.

findings.claim_in_file: "Inputs as walked through: **number of contributors ASSUMED = 2**; known contributor under HP = Twiggs's known sample; **known contributors under HD = left blank.**"
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The witness's immediately following explanation of why HD was blank is omitted. Counsel: "Is that because you didn't know what the defense hypothesis was?" Bakker: "No. Again, the defense hypothesis for this situation, if I'm comparing someone, is an unknown unrelated individual and that is taken into account during the calculation."
findings.why_it_matters: As printed, "left blank" sits adjacent to the file's second headline and reads as a defect in the run. The witness said the blank IS the unknown-unrelated hypothesis, applied by the software. Omitting it is the same one-directional pattern as the two findings above, in the passage that carries the most weight in the file.

findings.claim_in_file: "Pattern `/octillion|quintillion|quadrillion|…|billion/` over `day2.txt`, all 7 hits opened… **Zero occurrences in lines 5070–8862.**"
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The hit census is exactly right (2 Faumuina + 3 "quadrillion" in one Bakker answer + 2 prosecutor = 7), and the headline claim — that neither figure is uttered during Bakker's testimony-in-chief — is CONFIRMED. But the closing sentence is false for the pattern as stated: Bakker's three "quadrillion" utterances are at line 6899, inside 5070–8862 and inside her testimony-in-chief. The bullet contradicts its own breakdown.
findings.why_it_matters: A search null is a claim about the search. A downstream file relying on "zero occurrences" would wrongly conclude no magnitude figure of any kind appears in her direct. The fix is to scope the sentence to `/octillion|quintillion/`.

findings.claim_in_file: the court "repeatedly allow[ed] '**one more question**.'" — presented in quotation marks.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The phrase "one more question" does not appear anywhere in day2.txt (`grep -nE "one more question|single question"` returns one line only). The court's actual words are "I'll allow this single question as she may respond" (once) and "a limit of a limited number of questions." "One more" appears once as counsel's, not the court's: "One more and then we're—".
findings.why_it_matters: Quotation marks around a phrase not in the record. The substantive characterisation (the court repeatedly allowed a further question then reined it in) is accurate and survives if the marks come off or the real phrase is used.

findings.claim_in_file: "**a court staffer twice corrected 'Baker 35'**"
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Rev labels the corrector "Speaker 10," who appears exactly twice in the whole of day2.txt — both times in this four-second exchange — and is never addressed by name or role by anyone. No basis in the record identifies them as court staff rather than co-counsel, a paralegal, or the display operator counsel called "Kimberly."
findings.why_it_matters: Hazard 1 requires a stated basis before naming a person or role, normally the court addressing them in an adjacent turn. There is none here. "An unidentified speaker" carries the same analytic weight without the unsupported attribution.

findings.target_section: §2.8, second bullet of the items 1–6 discussion
findings.claim_in_file: "About **3 microliters** of extract remained after 10 were used, and **she agreed the remaining 3 would still yield nothing.**"
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: She did not agree with counsel's proposition. Q: "So if you didn't get any results with 10, what you left over would not be sufficient to get any sort of independent testing done, correct?" A: "**It could be tested.** However, my expectation, if I took 10 microliters and did not get any DNA, the remaining three would also still not give me any DNA."
findings.why_it_matters: The file's paraphrase collapses a refusal-plus-expectation into an agreement, and drops the half that cuts for the State on the destructive-testing point. Same one-directional compression pattern.

findings.claim_in_file: "She confirmed both the **NRC 1996** statement… and **FBI standard 7.4** on retaining or returning a portion." Items are described as "entirely consumed."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Her answer went further than confirmation: "That is correct. And **we do actually return the remaining extract**, the liquid from our DNA testing. So we did consume the swab, however, there was a small amount of liquid that was left and returned." Counsel probed "On some of the items, right?" — "**I believe on all of the items.**" Counsel then said "Well, we'll get to that in a minute" and never returned to it. Also unrecorded: the separate FBI quality-assurance standard requiring a written sample-consumption policy, put and confirmed.
findings.why_it_matters: "Entirely consumed" is the file's framing in §2.8 and again in §3.4 for Oliver. The witness's evidence that liquid extract was returned on all items is a direct qualifier to it, was expressly reserved for challenge by the defence, and was never challenged.

findings.claim_in_file: "**The backpack (item 9)**"
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Counsel said "a backpack, **which you labeled as Exhibit 9**" — an exhibit designator, not an item designator, silently converted by the file with no note. Day 2 independently contains a different "State's Exhibit 9" (a display exhibit shown to another witness) and an "Exhibit 9" in the court's victims'-rights ruling.
findings.why_it_matters: Steelman: "you labeled" points at her own report, which numbers items, so counsel probably misspoke. But the file's §1.4 undertakes to give the basis for every normalisation, and D-55 is specifically about exhibit-number collisions — and this is a live Day 2 "Exhibit 9" collision the file did not catch while asserting the conversion.

findings.claim_in_file: "the **five** isoallele locations charted"; and the locus written as "**THO1**".
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Counsel's own count is unstable across the argument and the questioning: "at this location and **five or six** others"; "in at least **five** separate locations"; "at the **six** different locations relevant to the comparison to Mr. Robinson"; "differences at these **five** locations"; "as you look at these **five** areas." The file states five flatly. Separately, the transcript reads "THO" once and only once; the file writes "THO1" twice (itself a non-standard rendering of TH01) and §1.4 does not list the normalisation, although it lists "TPOC's location = TPOX" for the same class of garble.
findings.why_it_matters: The file opens D-58 for exactly this kind of unreconciled count elsewhere in the same testimony; leaving this one unflagged is inconsistent, and the undisclosed locus normalisation breaks §1.4's stated promise that each garble carries its basis.

findings.claim_in_file: "**Item 55 — swabs of a stairwell railing — TWO SWABS COMBINED into one sample and consumed.** She did not inquire whether they came from different areas."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Two witness refusals of counsel's premises are omitted. (i) Q: "that was two swabs from a stairwell railing **where the suspect touched the railing**, right?" A: "**As far as I know, they were swabs from a stairwell**" — she declined the suspect-contact premise. (ii) Q: "And when you do that, you create a mixture, right?" A: "**I don't know that I would agree** that combining the two would create a mixture… However, I don't know that for certain." Her policy justification ("our policies and procedures is that we can combine those two together") is also dropped. Comparable omission in §2.6: asked "did you assume that at that location that the allele that dropped out matched his allele?" she answered "**At that location, no.**"
findings.why_it_matters: The last of these is directly load-bearing for §5.3: it is an on-record denial that she assumed dropped-out alleles matched the elimination donor. The file quotes the tail of her answer but not the question it denies, which makes a denial read as a deflection.

findings.claim_in_file: Records only her disclaimers: "I cannot give an opinion as far as activity level goes… I cannot give exact timing as to when DNA was deposited."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: On cross she gave affirmative mechanism and degradation evidence the file does not record: DNA reaches an object "via direct contact… also… via body fluids such as blood or **through transfer**. So if I were to touch an object and then that object is given to someone else, my DNA could potentially be on that other individual through the transfer of DNA"; degradation is normal and universal, affected by dirt and UV; and, on both exhibits, "Did that degradation affect your ability to reach a conclusion here?" — "**No, it did not**" (asked separately as to the screwdriver and as to the towel).
findings.why_it_matters: §3.4 records Oliver's household-transfer framing but the file records no secondary-transfer testimony from Bakker, though hers is more explicit. The degradation answers are the State's rehabilitation of the §2.6 partial-profile point and are absent.

findings.target_section: §1.1 / §2 (scope of the Bakker read); library-wide caveats
findings.claim_in_file: "`day2.txt` lines 5050–9640 (Bakker, complete: swearing-in through excusal)"; and §2's note that Bakker was called out of order, "interrupting Sgt. Faumuina's testimony. Faumuina stepped down still under oath."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Three end-of-block facts are unrecorded. (i) The court supplied three wall-clock anchors inside this block — "we are at the 4:30 point" (stream 07:36:52), "we are now at 4:40" (07:44:47), "It's 5:00" (08:07:22) — which track stream time with no jump across a ~30-minute unbroken stretch and fix the Day 2 late-afternoon offset to within ~2½ minutes. (ii) The excusal and adjournment: "May this witness be excused?" — "Yes" — "You may step down"; neither party wanted the benefit of the record; "we'll go ahead and be adjourned until tomorrow at 1:00 PM. **We do not have morning court for this proceeding.**" (iii) Faumuina did not resume on Day 2 — the day ended at Bakker's excusal.
findings.why_it_matters: (i) is an in-block, testable datum bearing on standing hazard 2, which was itself corrected on 2026-08-01 and which hazard 11 says must be re-tested rather than repeated; it CONFIRMS the corrected form (no jump; ±5 min conversion) for Day 2 afternoon and should be banked. (ii) is a checkable schedule fact the library does not have. (iii) closes the "out of order" narrative §2 leaves open.

findings.claim_in_file: "**Her explanation, in full, and it is the most important answer in her testimony:**" followed by a quotation containing three ellipses.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The quotation is accurate as to every word retained, but it is not the answer in full. Elided are her opening concession "I did" (agreeing she had concluded Twiggs was a contributor to BOTH items 7 and 8 despite the ratio of 1), "and the DNA, unlike that major contributor, he also had those peaks," and "So that was one proposition or one hypothesis that I determined that he was an assumed contributor. There are multiple different ways."
findings.locator: day2.txt 8113–8122 (Rev 07:21:11–07:22:03), spanning the PART 12 OF 14 seam
findings.why_it_matters: "In full" is a provenance claim about a quotation, and hazard 7 (selective quotation is reliable as to the words, never as to the document) is the reason it matters. The elided "I did" in fact strengthens the file's own point and should be restored.

findings.claim_in_file: "**Two competing in-laboratory attributions**, neither adopted by the testifying examiner"; D-56 titled "Two **competing** in-laboratory attributions of the backpack."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The two attributions are "potentially left behind by a bystander" (her account of what investigators later determined) and the log entry "The backpack belongs to Kirk's detailees" (recorded by another laboratory staffer). Both are in-laboratory records of investigator-supplied information and both point the same way on the only operative question — that the backpack was not the suspect's and no comparisons were needed. A person detailed to the victim's party is a bystander for that purpose.
findings.why_it_matters: "Competing" is an analyst-layer characterisation of two records that differ in specificity rather than in direction, and it is what makes the item a discrepancy-register entry at all. The underlying facts and the "neither adopted" caution are correctly stated; only the framing overreaches.

confirmations.claim: Headline 1 / §5.1 / D-53 — BOTH headline figures place Lance Twiggs in BOTH competing propositions. CONFIRMED, and independently twice. Faumuina reading State's Exhibit 31: item 7-1, "1.7 octillion times more likely if Twiggs and T. Robinson are contributors than if Twiggs and an unknown, unrelated person are contributors"; item 8-1, "30 quintillion times more likely if Twiggs and T. Robinson are contributors, than if Twiggs and an unknown, unrelated person are contributors." The prosecutor then read both sentences back to Bakker on cross and she assented to the reporting-language point on each. The file's rule that neither figure may appear without both propositions attached is fully carried by the record.

§2.1's architectural quote is verbatim and in context. "For example, if I'm utilizing someone as a known elimination sample, I will apply their DNA profile both to the HP and HD," immediately followed by counsel establishing HP = prosecution hypothesis and HD = defence hypothesis, both confirmed. This is the sentence the file calls "the whole architecture of both figures," and it carries that weight.

§2.2 — the likelihood ratio of one and the "uninformative" classification are verbatim and correctly characterised. Q: "what was the likelihood ratio that you calculated based on this chart?" A: "The likelihood ratio was one." Q: "So that doesn't rise to the level of even limited inclusion, correct?" A: "Correct. It would fall under an uninformative." Restated by her on the next page: "Based on the STRmix run, it was uninformative, but I did use my own knowledge and training…"

§2.2 — the six STRmix inputs are all confirmed exactly as the file lists them: report "dated September 15th" relating to "item 7-1"; "Assume there are two contributors"; evidence input "sample 7A"; known contributor under HP = "sample 61" = "Twiggs's known sample"; known contributors under HD "left that blank." The exhibit designation is also confirmed: "Baker 38, pages 39 through 44 is admitted and may be published."

§2.2 — the verbal scale is confirmed, including the internal inconsistency the file flags. Counsel: "you need to reach a likelihood ratio of two in order to get even limited support for an inclusion, correct?" — "Correct, yes." And, as transcribed, she assigned "very strong support for inclusion" to two adjacent bands (≥1,000,000 and 10,000-to-under-1,000,000) in consecutive sentences. The file's flag that this is resolvable only against page five of the report, not against the transcript, is right.

§2.2's guard — "She refused the 'excluded' framing, and that cuts for the State" — CONFIRMED. The compound question was "the result you got was that he was not a contributor, correct? Or that it was not even of limited value in including him?" and she answered only the second limb ("Based on the STRmix run, it was uninformative"). She repeated the refusal on redirect: to "you ignored it and decided otherwise, correct?" she answered "I did not ignore it."

§5.3's core scoped null CONFIRMED by line-by-line read of day2.txt 7750–9640: no alternative, unconditioned likelihood ratio for Tyler Robinson is computed, offered, or requested anywhere in this block. The only numerical likelihood ratios in the block are "one" (elimination donor, item 7-1), 1.7 octillion (item 7.1) and 30 quintillion (item 8.1). Also confirmed: the defence attack was on the PROPRIETY of the assumption, not on its magnitude — counsel's own framings are "whether the expert correctly concluded that Twiggs not was a possible contributor, but was a contributor" and "you didn't use it and rely upon it for your conclusion about Twiggs."

§2.6 — all three locus exchanges are verbatim and correctly summarised. D16: "Mr. Twiggs was a 912 at D16" / "The only piece of information I had for sample eight at item D16 was a 12." D19S: "It was a 1416" / "Did you find a 16 allele in the 8A sample?" — "No, I did not." THO: "He was a 79.3" / "Did you find a seven allele in the 8.1 sample?" — "No, I did not. But again, this is a mixture and there is some dropout." Her THO answer "there's only one individual represented there. So when comparing an elimination, I would essentially ignore that location" is verbatim. Her single-source-versus-mixture distinction, put from Butler's textbook, is also correctly recorded.

§2.6 — the close-of-direct quotation is verbatim: "Correct. I only utilize length differences, STRs in this case. The FBI laboratory does not use sequencing for nuclear DNA testing, nor am I qualified in it." Her NGS answer is also correctly characterised: the FBI uses next-generation sequencing for mitochondrial DNA but not for nuclear DNA.

§2.8 — the consumption inventory is verbatim and complete: "Items one through six… in addition to items 54 and 55, which were swabs of swiped finger areas and swabs of stairwell railing." The northeast-corner location of items 1–6 ("the loci building" = Losee), the null result ("you concluded that there was no DNA present on any of those items, correct?" — "That is correct"), the ~3 µL residue against 10 µL used, the combining and consumption of the two item-55 railing swabs, and the result "I got DNA from more than five individuals, so I could not provide a conclusion" are all confirmed as stated.

§2.8 — the NRC 1996 and FBI standard 7.4 confirmations are accurate, including that she agreed standard 7.4 is the FBI's own laboratory policy ("The FBI's lab policy?" — "Yes, it is"), and that destructive testing was requested before any samples were received ("Before you received any samples, did you request to perform what's called destructive testing…?" — "Yes, I did"; and that the determination was made "before you even saw any of the evidence" — "Yes").

§2.8 — the backpack passage is verbatim on both sides: "it was determined that that backpack was potentially left behind by a bystander and there was no comparisons needed at that time"; and "according to your notes at page 20, 'The backpack belongs to Kirk's detailees?'" — "Yes… That was not my communication log, that was someone else within the laboratory. That was the information that they received." The file's caution that neither attribution was adopted by the testifying examiner is right.

§2.10 — the Baker 34 / Baker 35 sequence is verbatim as the file reports the words: Burt moves "Baker 34" ("It's five pages"); the State objects on probable-cause relevance; the court admits Baker 34 with a time limit; Burt then moves the isoallele chart; the court asks "And is this Baker 34?"; Burt answers "Yes"; the unidentified speaker corrects "Baker 35" and then "35"; Burt adopts "35. Baker 35"; the State says "Same objection"; the court rules "I'll admit into evidence under the previous statement as it relates to Baker 34. It may be published." (Only the file's INTERPRETATION of the last sentence is reported as a finding above; the words themselves are confirmed.)

§2.10 — the DOJ ULTR designation point is confirmed: on cross the prosecutor called it "an Exhibit 8.4, Baker 8.4, which is the DOJ Ultra, which is the Uniform Language…" and the witness expanded it as "Uniform Language for Reporting and Testimony, I believe."

D-55(b) CONFIRMED within minutes on Day 2: the same FBI report is called "People's Exhibit 31" (07:16:38), "plaintiff's Exhibit 31" (07:17:04) and "Plaintiff's 31" (07:17:59) by the same counsel, and "Exhibit 31" by the prosecutor on cross. findings.target_section: §2.2, the block quote introduced as "Her explanation, in full"
findings.claim_in_file: "Her explanation, in full, and it is the most important answer in her testimony: 'I didn't utilize this calculation… I visually looked at the DNA sample… We don't have a threshold…'"
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The quotation is not in full — it carries two ellipses, and the first one removes the witness's affirmative evidentiary basis: "I visually looked at the DNA sample **and the DNA, unlike that major contributor, he also had those peaks. So that was one proposition or one hypothesis that I determined that he was an assumed contributor. There are multiple different ways.** We don't have a threshold…"
findings.why_it_matters: The elided clause is the only thing in the answer that states what she actually saw. Removing it while labelling the quote "in full" leaves the visual call looking groundless, which is the reading the defence was pressing. This is hazard 7 operating inside the file's single most-quoted passage, and it cuts one way only — against the witness.

findings.claim_in_file: The file records the report-language asymmetry ("you say that one of the contributors is Twiggs… — 'I do. And with elimination samples, that's slightly different.'") and lists four confirmed reporting limits.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: It omits Bakker's own spontaneous refusal of source language, and her express two-step distinction. Q: "you reached the determination that he was the source of both those samples, one of the sources, right?" A: "**I don't want to use the word source.** … So using the word assumed, that's verbiage that we use when we calculate our statistical calculation. I'm letting the software know I know this individual is there. I'm assuming that they're there. **Based on my comparisons I did see evidence that that person was there.**"
findings.why_it_matters: This is the strongest Bakker quotation in the whole transcript for the file's own living-persons header ("A DNA 'support for inclusion' statement is not a source attribution; both analysts said so expressly") and for §5.4, and it is missing while the Oliver equivalent is quoted twice. It also supplies the assumed-for-the-statistic vs seen-on-comparison distinction that §2.5's circularity note needs.

findings.target_section: §2.3 ("The elimination designation, and the towel") and §5.3, fourth clause
findings.claim_in_file: §5.3: "The defence never established that assuming an elimination contributor is improper practice rather than routine. Confidence: High."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The finding is correct, but the evidence that carries it is nowhere in §2.3. Bakker gave two unrebutted routine-practice analogies: the stolen-vehicle elimination ("if we have a stolen vehicle, I will request an elimination sample from the known driver… so I can subtract out their DNA to see what I have left over") and the sexual-assault consensual-partner elimination, given expressly as her reason for the asymmetric report language ("If I see that they're present, I can say they're present… It's different than comparing a known individual if they're an elimination sample").
findings.why_it_matters: The project's steelman rule requires the strongest reading to be shown before an entry is treated. §5.3 asserts the conclusion at High confidence while the recording layer omits both of the witness's justifications, so a reader cannot check the finding against the record. It also leaves §2.3's asymmetry paragraph reading as an unanswered charge when it was in fact answered.

findings.claim_in_file: "On the NIST 2024 report: 'we never truly know the number of contributors in a forensic sample… I'm making the best determination based on the DNA evidence that I have.'"

Unscoped, it invites the false inference that a Twiggs-alone statistic of 1 underwrites the 30 quintillion figure too, when for item 8-1 there is no such statistic on this record at all. findings.claim_in_file: "⚠ The court's admission ruling names the wrong exhibit… the judge's ruling then reads 'I'll admit into evidence under the previous statement as it relates to Baker 34.' An exhibit-identity defect created by the record itself, not by the transcription." D-55 calls (c) "the serious one."

The preceding turn is McBride's "Same objection, Your Honor," which is exactly what a same-reasoning ruling responds to.

findings.target_section: §2.5 analyst-layer note; repeated flatly in D-54
findings.claim_in_file: "The two-person call on item 7 was itself reached only by assuming Twiggs." D-54: "The two-person call is what defeats the PCAST 20% objection — and it was reached by assuming Twiggs."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Her stated route to the two-person call was a comparison, not a bare assumption: "I was submitted an elimination sample from Mr. Twiggs… **When I compared him to this sample, all of the DNA, unlike that major contributor, matched to Mr. Twiggs.** So because of that, I determined that there's actually only two individuals, **because those small peaks, there was nothing left for a third individual to be compared to.**" She separately refused the "assumed" label for the interpretive step while accepting it for the statistical step.
findings.why_it_matters: "Reached only by assuming Twiggs" is stronger than the record. The witness's account is that the third-contributor inference was retired because a comparison profile accounted for the residual sub-threshold peaks — a different and, on its face, evidentially grounded operation. findings.claim_in_file: "≥ 1,000,000 = 'very strong support for inclusion'; 2 is the floor for even 'limited support for an inclusion'; 1 is 'uninformative.'"
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The scale as described in court is two-sided and the second band is given numerically: counsel asks about "the **greater than one million less than one in a hundred**" column, and she gives "if I have a likelihood ratio that's greater than or equal to one million, I designate that as very strong support for inclusion. findings.target_section: §5.3, "Confidence: High that the record is silent on the consequence"
findings.claim_in_file: "The record does NOT establish that assuming Twiggs inflated the Robinson likelihood ratio… Confidence: High that the record is silent on the consequence."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: The core holds (verified: no unconditioned Robinson ratio is computed, offered or requested anywhere in 5040–9640). But the record is not wholly silent on magnitude, and what it contains runs toward the State: "if I originally interpret something as three, calculated statistic, **if that major contributor is the individual that I'm comparing to**, if I change the number of contributors to two, based on the studies and based on my own experience, **it doesn't change the likelihood ratio of that major contributor by much**" — and Robinson is the major contributor on both items (95% and 89%). §2.4 quotes the "by much" clause but drops the conditional that makes it applicable here.
findings.why_it_matters: §5.3 is expressly framed as an over-hedge guard running toward the State; stating "the record is silent" at High confidence understates the record in the same direction the guard exists to correct. The precise claim — silent as to the effect of the *conditioning*, but carrying affirmative testimony that the *NoC change* would not much move the major contributor's ratio — is both more accurate and stronger for the State.

findings.claim_in_file: "⚠ Item 55 — swabs of a stairwell railing — TWO SWABS COMBINED into one sample and consumed. She did not inquire whether they came from different areas."

(c) "Ordinary lab-practice colour, rightly cut for length." Fails on the file's own internal standard: §3.4 records precisely this distinction for the other analyst — "**Entirely consumed:** items 1.4, 1.6… **Extracts retained** (swabs consumed, liquid remaining): 1.1, 1.2…". The file plainly regards consumed-swab-versus-retained-extract as reportable, applies it to Oliver (ATF), and omits it for Bakker (FBI). That asymmetry, in a file that expressly governs on both witnesses, is a defect rather than editorial economy.
(d) "§5.5 is defensible shorthand." Survives in part, and this narrows the finding. "Produced nothing usable" is untouched — she agreed 3 µL against the 10 used would still yield no DNA (8482), and item 55 gave >5 contributors (8526). What does not survive is the flat clause "**and the samples are gone**" at **Confidence: High**, which the same witness qualifies twice in the same passage (8362; 8426).

TWO CORRECTIONS I MAKE TO THE FINDER'S OWN FRAMING, both of which the adopted wording must carry.
1. The finder writes that she was "asserting compliance with standard 7.4 on all items." That over-reads by one step. She never said "we complied with 7.4"; she said the extract is returned and "I believe on all of the items" — a hedged statement of belief. It amounts to a compliance claim only because 7.4 as read to her says "retain or return a portion of the evidence sample **or extract**" (8358). Recording layer and analyst layer must stay split here.
2. The finder omits evidence cutting back the other way, which I found and which must go in or the correction over-swings toward the State (hazard 4 runs in both directions): her own opening definition of destructive testing was "…subjecting it to testing, **so there's nothing remaining**" (8306). However…") before giving her rationale — so the rationale must not be quoted without the concession that precedes it.

NOT PRESENT ANYWHERE ELSE. The point is not made in another section, a caveat, the living-persons header, the register or the revision log; a library-wide grep for extract-return language returns only two unrelated CR-WATCH lines. CR-E06 expressly "governs on these two witnesses", so the omission is the library's omission.

Verdict: CONFIRMED, at material severity for §5.5's wording and §2.8's balance — not for any headline result.

findings.why_it_matters: Both directions are missing, which is why I grade this material rather than stylistic. As written, §2.5 has her "not practitioners" answer standing unanswered — the record shows counsel answering it within four questions with her own former unit chief — while also omitting the three answers in which she most directly refused the defence's premises. CLAUDE.md requires confirmations to be logged explicitly and requires the strongest reading of a claimant's position to be shown before anything resolves. §2.5 already carries a careful non-resolution; it needs the record on both sides underneath it.

findings.claim_in_file: §9: "**Partial STR genotype data spoken in open court is summarised, not reproduced.**" §2.6: "at **D16** Twiggs is 9,12 and item 8 yielded only a 12; at **D19S** he is 14,16 and no 16 was found; at **THO1** he is 7, 9.3 and no 7 was found."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: §2.6 reproduces three loci of Lance Twiggs's genotype, resolved by the file from the transcript's garbled "912", "1416" and "79.3" into the paired calls 9,12 / 14,16 / 7,9.3. The transcript also contains four loci for Tyler Robinson — DYS391 = 11, D3S1358 = 17,17, vWA = 18,19, TPOX = 8,9 — and the file reproduces none of them.
findings.why_it_matters: The residual-scope statement is false on its face, and unstated or misstated scope reads as coverage that does not exist. The asymmetry compounds it: the file reproduces partial genotype data for a private individual who is accused of nothing and testified under use immunity, while withholding the same class of data for the defendant — the reverse of the protective ordering the living-persons header sets up. I am not saying three loci is per se disclosive or that reproducing them was wrong: they are necessary to the defence's exclusion argument and §2.6 could not make its point without them. The defect is that §9 denies doing it, and that the file should either reproduce both or neither and say which.

findings.claim_in_file: "Pattern `/octillion|quintillion|quadrillion|…|billion/` over `day2.txt`, all 7 hits opened… **Zero occurrences in lines 5070–8862.**"
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: For the pattern as stated, the null is false and the same bullet concedes it two clauses earlier. day2.txt:6899 sits inside 5070–8862 and carries three occurrences of "quadrillion" — the very three the bullet describes as "Bakker's own hypothetical about STRmix variability." My grep for /octillion|quintillion|quadrillion/ returns 5 lines (4877, 4913, 6899, 9119, 9143) carrying 7 occurrences, which matches the file's count exactly. The heading claim — that the figures 1.7 octillion and 30 quintillion are never uttered during Bakker's testimony-in-chief — is CONFIRMED.
findings.why_it_matters: A search null is a claim about the search (standing hazard 5), and this one is internally contradictory as written: the range sentence contradicts the hit accounting in the same bullet. The substantive conclusion survives; the sentence needs to name the narrower pattern it is actually true of — "zero occurrences of /octillion|quintillion/ in lines 5070–8862."

findings.claim_in_file: "each time you run the software, you will get a different number… **you will never get the same answer twice, but it will be no more than a magnitude of 10**" — presented as one quotation.
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: These are two answers separated by two intervening question-and-answer turns and about 25 seconds. The first is at day2.txt:6875, the second at day2.txt:6891, with "But it does change it, correct?" / "Yes" and a further question between them.
findings.why_it_matters: A bare ellipsis inside a single quotation normally signals elision within one utterance, not a splice across a Q&A boundary. Selective quotation is reliable as to the words and never as to the document (standing hazard 7), and this project quotes minimally and precisely by rule. The meaning is not distorted here, which is why this is minor — but the same splice convention applied to an adversarial exchange would be.

findings.claim_in_file: "…and **she agreed the remaining 3 would still yield nothing**"; and "She **requested and received** permission for **destructive testing before receiving any samples.**"
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: On the first: she did not agree it would yield nothing — she said it could be tested and gave an expectation. "It could be tested. However, my expectation, if I took 10 microliters and did not get any DNA, the remaining three would also still not give me any DNA." On the second: the record has the request, not the grant. "I have to request permission to consume prior to doing so, and I did in this case." No grant is stated; it is inferable from the fact of consumption but is not on the record.
findings.why_it_matters: Both flatten a hedge out of the witness's answer in the direction that strengthens the defence's destructiveness point — the mirror image of the over-hedging the file guards against elsewhere. §5.5 is graded Confidence High and rests on this paragraph. Small, but this file's whole method is that a grade traces to what was actually said.

findings.claim_in_file: "**She agreed both samples had minor contributors below 20%:** item 7 at **5%/95%**, item 8 at **11%/89%**."
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Her answer for item 7 carries a qualifier the file drops, and it is the most direct statement of the conditioning thesis anywhere in her direct: "Yes, it was. **For one of the runs when I compared to Mr. Robinson conditioning on Mr. Twiggs**, it was a 5% to 95%." The phrase "conditioning on Mr. Twiggs" is not quoted anywhere in CR-E06.
findings.why_it_matters: §5.1 rests on "if I'm utilizing someone as a known elimination sample, I will apply their DNA profile both to the HP and HD" (day2.txt:7548), which the file quotes and which I confirm. But this second sentence says it in the concrete — the witness naming the actual run for item 7 as a Robinson comparison conditioned on Twiggs. It is a free confirmation of the file's own strongest finding, in the witness's own words, left on the table. Dropping the qualifier also makes 5%/95% read as a single property of item 7 rather than the output of one particular conditioned run.

findings.claim_in_file: "**The defence's counter was that the court had already ruled it retains the ultimate determination of the RELIABILITY of Rule 1102 hearsay, which it called 'the law of this case.'**"
findings.what_the_transcript_shows: Accurate as far as it goes, but the same answer records a prior constitutional challenge that appears nowhere else in the file: "when we objected to the hearsay aspect of these DNA reports and other reports, you ruled that you are the ultimate determiner of the reliability of the hearsay evidence being admitted. You will recall that our argument was **the statute was unconstitutional because it was dictating that you find certain evidence to be reliable without considering whether it was reliable.** Your ruling, as I understood it, was no, you retain the ultimate determination." The State's answering authority is also unrecorded: "Under Rule 1102(b)(4) the Exhibit 31 is considered reliable hearsay."
findings.why_it_matters: §8 lists ten acquisition targets and none is the prior ruling on the constitutionality of the hearsay statute — which, on the defence's own account, is the ruling that makes reliability justiciable at this hearing at all, and therefore the predicate for the entire Bakker examination. It belongs in §8 as a Tier 1 target.

confirmations.claim: §2.1 — both headline figures are quoted accurately and both propositions do contain Lance Twiggs. Item 7-1: "Male DNA was obtained from Item 7, sub 1. Item 7, sub 1 was interpreted as originating from two individuals, one of whom is Twiggs. The DNA results from Item 7, sub 1 and what are 1.7 octillion times more likely if Twiggs and T. Robinson are contributors than if Twiggs and an unknown, unrelated person are contributors." Item 8-1 is verbatim as the file has it. The file's bracketed "[are]" for the garble "and what are" is an honest, marked normalisation. The claim under attack target (a) — that both figures place Twiggs in BOTH propositions — is CONFIRMED on the face of the text read into the record.

§2.1 — the figures were read by Sgt. Jennifer Faumuina, from the report, BEFORE Bakker was called, and she is functionally the witness (answering counsel's "if you'll read Item 7.1…"). Her rank is confirmed independently three ways: the State's preview ("a sergeant with the SBI"), her own answer ("I'm currently a sergeant within the State Bureau of Investigation"), and the court addressing her as "Sergeant."

§2 — "Faumuina stepped down still under oath" is CONFIRMED verbatim by the court: "Sergeant, if you'd like to step down, you're still under oath, and so please don't discuss your testimony with anyone." I initially suspected this was unsupported because the judge says "Agent" nine lines later; the earlier turn settles it.

§2.1 — "Item 7 = 'Towel from around Mauser or rifle, Serial Number 8863.'" CONFIRMED verbatim as read into the record. "Item 8 = 'Screwdriver from perch'" is confirmed from Bakker's own words ("Item 8 was the screwdriver from the perch") and the State's description of item 8-1 as "swabs of the handle area of the screwdriver."

§2.1 — the conditioning mechanism is stated by the witness in the terms the file quotes: "if I'm utilizing someone as a known elimination sample, I will apply their DNA profile both to the HP and HD." She had just defined HP as the prosecution hypothesis and HD as the defence hypothesis, and confirmed HD is "an unknown unrelated individual." §5.1's structural claim is CONFIRMED.

§2.2 — the likelihood ratio of one and its classification are CONFIRMED verbatim, including the threshold. "So you need to reach a likelihood ratio of two in order to get even limited support for an inclusion, correct?" — "Correct, yes." Then: "what was the likelihood ratio that you calculated based on this chart?" — "The likelihood ratio was one." — "So that doesn't rise to the level of even limited inclusion, correct?" — "Correct. It would fall under an uninformative." She repeated it: "Based on the STRmix run, it was uninformative." Attack target (b) is CONFIRMED as to the value, the classification and the sub-2 threshold; only its item-scope is defective (see findings).

§2.2 — the file's own ⚠ guard "She refused the 'excluded' framing, and that cuts for the State" is CONFIRMED, and the compound question is described accurately. Q: "when you ran Mr. Twiggs' sample through STRmix, the result you got was that he was not a contributor, correct? Or that it was not even of limited value in including him?" A: "Based on the STRmix run, it was uninformative, but I did use my own knowledge and training to determine that I was going to utilize him as an assumed contributor." She answered only the second limb, exactly as the file says.

§2.2 — the verbal-scale internal inconsistency is CONFIRMED verbatim: "if I have a likelihood ratio that's greater than or equal to one million, I designate that as very strong support for inclusion. The next example, 10,000 to less than one million, I would say that's very strong support for inclusion and so forth." Two adjacent bands, same label, as transcribed. The file's judgement that this is resolvable only against page five of the report and not against the transcript is sound.

§2.2 — the Baker 38 inputs are CONFIRMED item by item: exhibit "Baker 38, page 39 through 44" (six pages), "dated September 15th," relating to "item 7- 1"; "Assume there are two contributors" — "Correct, yes"; input sample 7A as "just the raw data"; known contributor under HP = "sample 61" = "Twiggs's known sample"; known contributors under HD "you left that blank" — "Correct."

§5.3 — the core of the over-hedge guard is CONFIRMED. No alternative, unconditioned likelihood ratio for Robinson was computed, offered or requested anywhere I read or searched. Searched day2.txt lines >5050 with /without (mr\.? )?twiggs|if you (had not|hadn't)|not assum|unconditioned|without assuming|rerun|re-run/ — two hits, both counsel's argument about the number-of-contributors input, neither a request for an unconditioned ratio. Scope: my full read covers 5050–8548; beyond that I opened only targeted hits. The witness's answer that cuts for the State on magnitude is also confirmed: for a major contributor, changing NoC from three to two "doesn't change the likelihood ratio of that major contributor by much."

D-57 — CONFIRMED exactly as described, including that it happens inside a single question-and-answer pair. Q: "I think you said the ratio was 11% from the minor and 89% from the major. Is that Twiggs being the 11% and Robinson being the 89%?" A: "Yes. Twiggs better aligned with that 11% contributor and Mr. Robinson better aligned with that 79% contributor." The direct gives item 8 as "11% and… approximately 89%." The file's disposition ("probably trivial… a live trap for any file quoting the later line") is right.

D-58 — the arithmetic half is CONFIRMED and needs no external source. She gave the kit as "21 different locations… in addition to three sex determining locations" and then "We're looking at 21 and three sex type determining, so 24 total." "All 23 locations" appears twice, once in counsel's question and once in her own answer, exactly as the file states. The DYS385/DYS391 pair is also confirmed as transcribed.

§2.6 — the three loci where the elimination donor's own types were absent from item 8 are CONFIRMED verbatim, and the file's garble resolution is validated by counsel's own follow-ups treating each as two alleles. D16: "Mr. Twiggs was a 912 at D16" / "The only piece of information I had for sample eight at item D16 was a 12." D19S: "It was a 1416" / "Did you find a 16 allele in the 8A sample?" — "No, I did not." THO1: "He was a 79.3" / "Did you find a seven allele" — "No, I did not." Her mixture-versus-single-source distinction and "I would essentially ignore that location" are both quoted accurately.

§2.4 — the NoC sequence is CONFIRMED on every date and name. Original three "somewhere around September 12th"; "I changed my conclusion on September 13th of 2025"; the reviewer "concluded that she would have called it a number of contributor of two… And she said she agreed with me calling it three"; "approved by Tara Benson, is that the reviewer-" — "Yes, it is." The stated cause quotation is verbatim. The 150 RFU analytical threshold and her use of sub-threshold peaks for NoC are both confirmed.

§2.7 — all four reporting limits are CONFIRMED verbatim with the right answers attached: absolute identification ("Correct. No, I did not."), reasonable degree of scientific certainty ("That is correct. I was not."), zero error rate / infallible ("I am not, no."), and likelihood ratio of any magnitude / source attribution ("No, I'm not."). Her activity-level and timing limits are also verbatim, including "just because DNA is on an item doesn't necessarily mean that an individual touched it or utilized that item" and the 40-and-50-year persistence example.

§2.10 — the Tab 8 finding is CONFIRMED and correctly counted. The DOJ ULTR probabilistic-genotyping policy was displayed witness-only ("No, not on the big screen" / "This is just for the witness"), was never moved or admitted, and exactly two substantive provisions were read from it: the "support for inclusion" definition and the prohibition on asserting that a likelihood ratio of any magnitude provides an absolute identification or source attribution. By contrast Bakker 7 — the FBI "Approved Standards for Scientific Testimony and Reports for Autosomal DNA Testing" — was moved, objected to on relevance, admitted and published to the courtroom and the camera.

§2 ⚠ — the qualifications claim is CONFIRMED by search. Degree, accreditation (ANAB), the two-year training programme, oral and written board examinations, moot court, the competency exam and proficiency testing appear in day2.txt only from line 8886 onward, on the State's cross. Nothing of that kind appears between 5050 and 8862; the defence's direct establishes only employer, unit, location, tenure ("a little more than 10 years") and duties.

§2.8 — the consumption inventory is CONFIRMED verbatim, including that it was she who listed it: "Items one through six… in addition to items 54 and 55, which were swabs of swiped finger areas and swabs of stairwell railing." Items 1–6 as "taken from the northeast corner of the loci building" (the Losee garble), consumed, "no DNA present on any of those items," ~3 microliters remaining of 10 used. Item 55: two swabs combined, "They were both labeled as coming from the same stairwell and they were packaged together," result "I got DNA from more than five individuals, so I could not provide a conclusion."

§2.5 — the PCAST anchors are CONFIRMED verbatim: the 20% conclusion as counsel read it ("That sounds accurate, yes"), her three-or-more gloss ("PCAST called into question mixtures of three or more individuals with that minor or that low level contributor making up 20% or less"), the two mixture proportions, and her rebuttal ("That is true, but in this case it was also only a mixture of two individuals"). Her "not practitioners" answer is also verbatim, though counsel's question said "experts in your field" rather than "practitioners."

§2.9 — the court's posture is CONFIRMED. State v. Ramirez, 2012 UT 59 ¶10 is quoted closely enough to be checkable and the file's excerpt matches. "whether we walk one mile or a hundred miles down the path" is verbatim. "The law of this case" is correctly attributed to defence counsel, not to the court. The pattern the file describes holds across all eight objections in my range: the State's 702/scope objections were overruled twice and sustained in part twice, every defence exhibit offered on direct was admitted over relevance objection, and §2.9's ⚠ "NO ruling was made on the reliability of the DNA evidence at any point" is confirmed for this block.

§2.5's ⚠ analyst-layer note — "She also testified she did not calculate the proportions personally — STRmix produces them" — is CONFIRMED: "I did not calculate that personally… During that process, it does give an estimate of the breakdown of those potential contributors."

Living persons — no defect found on this axis in my block beyond the two logged above. Nothing in §2 states or implies that Lance Twiggs, Matthew Robinson or Amber Robinson did anything; every elimination-donor reference is attributed to the witness or to investigators and adopted by no one; "support for inclusion" is never rendered as "DNA was found on"; the roommate fact is carried inside her attributed answer ("from what I recall in speaking with the investigators"); and the "found in a bush out at the university" location appears once in the transcript, in counsel's question, and the file presents it as what she was asked rather than as fact. No address, contact detail or other identifying information about any private individual appears in the block or in the file's §2.

Method — tsearch.py self-validated on this run ("✓ method validated — known positive /use pliers/ found in day4.txt") before I relied on any null, per standing hazard 5. Every grep hit reported above was opened and read in context, and speakers were identified functionally (question versus answer, argument versus ruling) rather than from Rev labels, per standing hazard 1.
